notations: Y_purify = Q o C o R o E o Z

sources.note: Reframes purification/Moksha not as adding knowledge but as a multidimensional transformation: dimension expansion (D_t subset D_{t+1}) plus dimension refinement (v_t(d) preceq_d v_{t+1}(d)) under per-dimension order relations. Proposes six candidate operators E(xpansion), R(efinement), C(orrection), X (contradiction resolution), Q(ualify), Z(ero detection), studies their non-commutative composition algebra (closure/associativity/non-commutativity, e.g. E o Q != Q o E), reframes Yoga as operator composition trajectories (Y_purify = Q o C o R o E o Z), argues purification is a partially-ordered trajectory not a scalar purity score, and reformulates Moksha as Moksha = lim_{t->T} Purify(K_t) rather than max(K), posing a 5-question Epistemic Purification Algebra research programme.

The purification-as-multidimensional-quality-transformation hypothesis, first proposed in B0054; reused and substantially extended throughout B0055's kernel-model track (dimension/value/topology/probability formulations).

rows.anchor: Purification = Dimension Expansion + Dimension Refinement
rows.statement: Purification(K_t)->K_{t+1} should not mean simply adding more knowledge; it means transforming a knowledge state to become richer in relevant dimensions and more qualified/coherent/reliable/discriminating along them. Formalized as Dimension Expansion (D_t subset D_{t+1}, discovering/incorporating additional relevant dimensions) plus Dimension Refinement (for existing dimension d, v_t(d) -> v_{t+1}(d), quality/value along that dimension increases). Knowledge state reconceived as K_t=(D_t,V_t,R_t,P_t,...) rather than a set of facts.

rows.anchor: Every purification dimension requires an explicit ordering or transformation semantics.
rows.statement: Cannot assume v_{t+1} > v_t is always improvement ('higher is not always better'): e.g. uncertainty may decrease, provenance completeness may increase, contradiction may decrease, evidence quality/relevance/confidence may increase, but raw information quantity could increase while epistemic quality decreases. Each dimension d needs its own order relation preceq_d, with v_t(d) preceq_d v_{t+1}(d) meaning improvement per that dimension's declared ordering. Connects directly to the unresolved Step 287 issue that not every Sigma axis has a natural order (Acquisition A flagged as already problematic); states as a research requirement that every purification dimension requires an explicit ordering or transformation semantics.

rows.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t
rows.statement: Six candidate (not canonical) operators: E (Expansion) discovers a new relevant dimension d not-in D_t, now in D_{t+1}; R_d (Refinement) improves an existing dimension, v_t(d) prec_d v_{t+1}(d); C (Correction) changes an existing value because new evidence shows the previous state was wrong -- explicitly Purification != monotonic accumulation, since a purified state may contain less due to removed erroneous knowledge; X (Contradiction resolution) given p and not-p, the kernel must not arbitrarily select one, producing a conflict-qualified state until Buddhi/evidence/qualification can discriminate; Q (Qualification), the unresolved G1 operator, determining sufficient justification for the intended epistemic purpose, reframed via the recent Cavell-derived reconsideration so purification can mean correctly recognizing a gap cannot currently be resolved rather than resolving it; Z (Zero detection) detects epistemic absence, Z(K_t)->G_t (recognized gaps), with G_t transformable via E,R,C,Q into G_{t+1} -- the system becomes more purified partly by knowing more accurately what it does not know.

rows.anchor: E\circ Q \neq Q\circ E ... This is potentially a non-commutative epistemic algebra.
rows.statement: Buddhi reframed as an operator-selection mechanism B(K_t,O_t)->which transformation (from {E,R,C,X,Q,Z,...}) is appropriate, rather than another knowledge dimension -- 'the Kernel is not merely storing knowledge, it continuously discriminates what epistemic operation should happen next'. Yoga reframed as operator composition Y = O_n o ... o O_1, e.g. Y_purify = Q o C o R o E o Z (detect absence -> discover dimension -> refine/correct -> qualify -> new state) vs Y_conflict = Q o X o C. Proposes studying the resulting algebra's closure, associativity, and (expected) non-commutativity, e.g. E o Q != Q o E because discovering a dimension before qualification differs from qualifying before discovering it -- hypothesized as a non-commutative epistemic algebra.

rows.anchor: Moksha = \lim_{t\rightarrow T} \operatorname{Purify}(K_t)
rows.statement: Purification should be modelled as a partially ordered trajectory K_0->K_1->...->K_n (respecting Step 287's product-order finding), not a scalar purity score P(K_t); K_2 may be better than K_1 in some dimensions but incomparable in others. Purification defined formally as K_t->K_{t+1} when the transformation increases epistemic adequacy via D_{t+1} superset-or-equal D_t and/or for-all d in D_t, v_t(d) preceq_d v_{t+1}(d), while allowing correction (false(p)->removed/reclassified) and qualification (unknown->explicitly unknown) -- so purification is epistemic-adequacy-monotonic under an appropriate partial order, not information-monotonic. Correspondingly rejects Moksha=max(K); proposes instead Moksha = lim_{t->T} Purify(K_t), where the limit might mean dimensional completeness relative to a declared horizon, maximal epistemic qualification, minimal unresolved error, maximal justified value across relevant dimensions, or a change of epistemic regime -- explicitly leaving well-definedness of this limit to mathematics, not philosophy, to determine.

rows.anchor: Epistemic Purification Algebra ... five questions
rows.statement: Proposes structuring the next mathematical investigation as an 'Epistemic Purification Algebra' research programme with five questions: (1) what exactly is a knowledge dimension, (2) what does 'value' mean for each dimension, (3) which operators transform dimensions and values, (4) what algebraic laws govern composition of those operators, (5) does repeated purification converge toward a meaningful epistemic limit -- only after answering these should Moksha's formal role be assessed. Envisions KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind becoming computationally interpretable: Buddhi chooses epistemic operators, Yoga composes them, purification is the resulting trajectory through multidimensional Knowledge State space.

rows.anchor: Sentence \rightarrow \text{proposition about a dimension} ... Sentence can instantiate a knowledge dimension
rows.statement: Rejects sentence=dimension; a sentence should instead be treated as a proposition about a dimension, which under certain conditions instantiates a knowledge dimension. Worked example: 'Water boils at 100C at standard atmospheric pressure' does not itself define the dimension d=boiling point of water under specified pressure; rather the sentence supplies a value v(d)=100C, giving Dimension d + Value v + Context c.

rows.anchor: Sentence \neq \text{Proposition} \neq \text{Dimension}
rows.statement: Distinguishes Sentence != Proposition != Dimension via example: sentence s='Buddhi distinguishes' -> proposition p='Buddhi performs discrimination' -> dimension d='discrimination capability' -> value v(d) in {high,low,unknown} or later v(d) in [0,1]; a second sentence ('Buddhi should distinguish the permanent from the impermanent') can modify the same dimension d, so many sentences can contribute to one dimension. Prescribes a disciplined pipeline: Sentence -> Proposition -> Semantic interpretation -> Candidate dimension -> Dimension definition -> Evidence/context -> Value, to keep the Gita programme scientifically disciplined (a dimension must not be chosen merely because it sounds philosophically appropriate).

rows.anchor: \text{Sentence addition} \rightarrow \begin{cases}\text{new dimension}\\\text{new value}\\\text{new context}\\\text{new relation}\\\text{correction}\\\text{qualification}\end{cases}
rows.statement: Reframes the purification model: adding a new sentence's important effect is often D_1>D_0 (a new dimension is discovered) rather than |K_1|>|K_0| (more propositions), and further evidence can separately improve the value of an existing dimension v_0(d)->v_1(d); yields a small operator taxonomy that sentence addition maps to: new dimension, new value, new context, new relation, correction, or qualification -- described as exactly the operator algebra sought.

lineage_claims.quote: This is exactly the kind of operator algebra we were looking for.

rows.anchor: "One sentence may reveal or instantiate one or more knowledge dimensions." a **research hypothesis**, not a canonical rule
rows.statement: Proposes as a testable, falsifiable research hypothesis (not canonical rule): 'one sentence may reveal or instantiate one or more knowledge dimensions'; recommends testing it against a substantial corpus of Gita statements and ordinary KnowledgeOS knowledge -- if the same sentence routinely contains multiple independent dimensions, this falsifies a simplistic one-sentence/one-dimension model, and the experiment could lead to a rigorous Knowledge Atom -> Dimension -> Value -> Purification Operator definition chain.

experiment.hypothesis: One sentence may reveal or instantiate one or more knowledge dimensions.
experiment.setup: Collect a substantial corpus of Gita statements and ordinary KnowledgeOS knowledge sentences.
experiment.assumptions: Dimensions can be identified via the Sentence->Proposition->Dimension pipeline.
experiment.inputs: Gita sentences and KnowledgeOS corpus sentences.
experiment.method: For each sentence, identify how many independent dimensions it instantiates.
experiment.interpretation: If sentences routinely contain multiple independent dimensions, the one-sentence/one-dimension model is falsified.
experiment.limitations: Requires a disciplined, non-post-hoc dimension-identification procedure to avoid confirmation bias.
experiment.conclusion: Not yet concluded; proposed as next step.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} \succeq_{Pareto} K_t \iff \forall d:\ v_{t+1}(d) \text{ no worse} \ \wedge\ \exists d:\ \text{strictly better}
rows.statement: S2226's refusal of v_{t+1}>v_t ('higher is not always better': uncertainty may decrease, provenance completeness may increase, contradiction may decrease) is formally a Pareto-dominance problem: K_{t+1} succeq_Pareto K_t iff for all dimensions d, v_{t+1}(d) is no worse, and for some d, strictly better -- a Pareto order is a partial order admitting incomparable states by construction. Identified as the FIFTH independent route (of five distinct methods: Sigma-axis-order measurement per Step 291 finding 0 of 5 axes ordered; retraction non-monotonicity per Step 288/06; two separate corpus refusals to claim a semilattice, Steps 060 sec60.71 and 061/274.32; and now this Pareto argument) all converging on: there is no total order on K -- assessed as among the best-supported negative results in the programme.

lineage_claims.quote: refuses the obvious ordering, unprompted

rows.anchor: Moksha \sim transcendence of the conditioning regime ... G_t\rightarrow G_{\perp}
rows.statement: Revises the earlier Moksha formulation (Delta_t -> 0) given Chapter 14: Moksha != maximum K and Moksha != maximum Sattva; instead Moksha ~ transcendence of the conditioning regime, formalized as the research placeholder G_t -> G_perp meaning 'outside the three-mode conditioning model' -- explicitly flagged as a KnowledgeOS mathematical placeholder, not a Gita term. Proposes a purification trajectory Tamas-dominant -> (discrimination/clarification) -> Rajas-dominant -> (disciplined activity) -> Sattva-dominant -> (transcendence) -> Guna-atita, and a candidate epistemic-state model E_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,N_t) with N_t -Buddhi-> o_t and K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t).

lineage_claims.quote: I would now not use that as the sole definition.

rows.anchor: \Delta\text{Knowledge} = \Delta\text{Dimension} + \Delta\text{Quality} ... Knowledge Growth requires Discrimination
rows.statement: Distinguishes dimension from value: a statement could add a new dimension but have poor epistemic quality, or add no new dimension yet dramatically improve reliability/consistency/provenance/resolution/confidence/contextual understanding -- decomposed (as a research decomposition only) as Delta Knowledge = Delta Dimension + Delta Quality. Argues K_{t+1}>K_t in quantity does not imply K_{t+1} succ K_t epistemically, because more information != better knowledge; the kernel therefore requires Buddhi to discriminate: Knowledge Growth requires Discrimination, not merely ingestion.

rows.anchor: M\neq K_{\max} ... M\neq |\mathcal K|\rightarrow\infty ... M\sim\text{transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon}
rows.statement: With Chapters 11-14 combined, refuses modeling Moksha as the final Knowledge State: M != K_max and M != |K|->infinity. Proposes instead M ~ transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon, combined with Chapter 14's transcendence of ordinary conditioning; the theoretical transition is not simply K_0->K_1->K_2->... but (N,K_t,rho_t,G_t,Omega) -> different epistemic regime.

lineage_claims.quote: I would not model Moksha as the final Knowledge State.

rows.anchor: Knowledge quantity \neq Knowledge quality ... Purification \neq accumulation
rows.statement: Refines purification: P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} must not assume P(Sigma_t)>Sigma_t (per Step 287's finding that axes lack fully declared orders); instead a desired property Q(Sigma_{t+1})>=Q(Sigma_t) is wanted where Q is a future epistemic-quality functional that does not yet exist (an important research gap). Illustrates via example that K_1={1000 unsupported claims} could contain more information than K_2={100 well-supported claims} yet K_2 may be epistemically superior -- so Knowledge quantity != Knowledge quality, and Purification != accumulation; the kernel should maximize epistemic adequacy, not raw knowledge.
missing: formal definition of the epistemic-quality functional Q

rows.anchor: confidence: 0.9\rightarrow0.4 could actually represent epistemic improvement ... Purification \neq monotonic increase of every metric
rows.statement: Sharpens the non-monotonicity of purification with a concrete numeric example: confidence going from 0.9 to 0.4 could represent epistemic improvement if new evidence shows the previous certainty was unjustified. Hence Purification != monotonic increase of every metric; Purification = progress toward a better-qualified epistemic state. Proposes P(K_t,E_t,B_t)=K_{t+1} performing: remove unsupported claims, resolve contradictions, separate observation from interpretation, identify missing evidence, reduce unjustified certainty, preserve provenance, incorporate valid new evidence, identify new dimensions. Also defines a transformation-quality functional Q_B(K_t,K_{t+1}) assessing whether a transition reduces contradiction, reduces unsupported assertions, makes uncertainty explicit, improves provenance, increases justified knowledge, detects hidden gaps, or avoids introducing unsupported claims -- assessed as more promising than trying to mathematically encode 'good' and 'evil'.

rows.anchor: Knowledge growth ... Knowledge expansion ... Knowledge purification ... These are not equivalent.
rows.statement: Explicitly rejects Purification=increase-in-dimensions-and-values as the canonical mathematical definition (confidence 0.95->0.55 can represent improvement if the original confidence was unjustified): Purification != monotonic increase; P(K_t,K_{t+1}) = improvement in epistemic quality, with quality itself still needing formal definition. Distinguishes three non-equivalent concepts: Knowledge growth (K_t->K_{t+1}, a state change occurs); Knowledge expansion (dim(K_{t+1})>dim(K_t), new dimensions represented); Knowledge purification (P(K_t,K_{t+1})=true, epistemic quality improves) -- more information does not imply better knowledge, and knowledge expansion != knowledge purification, assessed as an important theoretical safeguard. Also reformulates purification against Sigma as Sigma_t --B,Q,delta--> Sigma_{t+1} with P(Sigma_t,Sigma_{t+1}) rather than a scalar purity score, given Step 287's problem with total ordering.

lineage_claims.quote: I would now reject that as the canonical mathematical definition.

rows.anchor: Purification \approx reduction of epistemic distortion ... K_{t+1}\not\supseteq K_t does not imply deterioration.
rows.statement: Rejects purification=increasing knowledge dimensions/values as the primary definition; proposes Purification ~ reduction of epistemic distortion, not more information. Example: K_t with P=verified becomes K_{t+1} with P=uncertain because new evidence shows the prior verification was inadequate -- numerically less certainty, epistemically better. Hence K_{t+1} not-superset-or-equal K_t does not imply deterioration.

lineage_claims.quote: I would now reject that as the primary definition.

rows.anchor: Q(K_{t+1}) > Q(K_t) ... 100 pieces of noisy knowledge \downarrow purification \downarrow 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge
rows.statement: From 5.11 (purification through disciplined action without attachment): sharpens purification from |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| to Q(K_{t+1})>Q(K_t) where Q is a future epistemic-quality function. Concrete illustration: a kernel could transform 100 pieces of noisy knowledge into 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge, becoming better despite becoming smaller -- assessed as a major correction to a purely information-quantity model.

rows.anchor: J_t = w_A A_t+ w_S S_t+ w_R R_t+ w_V V_t+ w_C C_t - \lambda Z_t - \mu U_t
rows.statement: Proposes, explicitly non-canonical/for research purposes only, a candidate kernel objective function J_t = w_A A_t + w_S S_t + w_R R_t + w_V V_t + w_C C_t - lambda Z_t - mu U_t (weighted five Sigma axes minus unresolved-gap term Z minus unjustified-commitment term U), with purification meaning J_{t+1}>J_t -- explicitly not adopted because the measurement scales and per-axis ordering remain unresolved (per Step 287). Proposes Moksha as the limiting condition where repeated purification cycles reach Delta J -> 0 (the kernel can no longer improve the state under the available epistemic horizon) -- a philosophical hypothesis, not an architecture decision.
missing: definitions of per-axis scales, orderings, and weights

assumptions.statement: the five Sigma axes and Z, U can be meaningfully combined via a weighted linear scalarization
assumptions.anchor: we should not yet adopt this equation because the measurement scales and ordering of the five axes remain unresolved.

rows.anchor: \mathcal P(K_t) = (D_t,Q_t,S_t,-X_t)
rows.statement: Refines purification from 'increasing dimensions + increasing values' to a four-component vector P(K_t)=(D_t,Q_t,S_t,-X_t) where D_t=epistemic dimensional coverage, Q_t=quality/value of knowledge, S_t=stability of discrimination, X_t=epistemic distortion (subtracted). Illustrated by a worked example: five conflicting claims P,P',P'',P''',P'''' reduce in number after Buddhi labels them [supported]/[superseded]/[unsupported]/[contradicted]/[unknown], with the number of claims decreasing while epistemic quality increases -- reinforcing Knowledge growth != knowledge purification. Explicitly connects to but does not yet merge with the existing Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C), to avoid premature formulation-merging per Steps 285-287.
missing: formal merge or non-merge determination with Sigma

lineage_claims.quote: I would now refine this after Chapter 2.

rows.anchor: Purification \neq information accumulation ... Purification = improvement of discrimination over the knowledge state ... (K_t,B_t,M_t)\rightarrow(K_{t+1},B_{t+1},M_{t+1})
rows.statement: Purification model corrected: not K_t -> K_{t+1} with increasing dimensions/values, and explicitly Purification != information accumulation. Instead Purification = improvement of discrimination over the knowledge state, formalized as the joint transition (K_t,B_t,M_t) -> (K_{t+1},B_{t+1},M_{t+1}).

lineage_claims.target: previous purification model (K_t -> K_{t+1} with increasing dimensions and values)
lineage_claims.quote: Your previous purification model was approximately: K_t \rightarrow K_{t+1} with increasing dimensions and values.

rows.anchor: Purification = improvement of epistemic quality ... clarity up, unsupported claims down, unresolved contradictions down, provenance quality up, discrimination quality up ... rather than merely |K_{t+1}| > |K_t| ... more knowledge != more statements ... KnowledgeOS should maintain epistemic readiness ... uncertainty -> observation -> understanding -> discrimination -> qualification -> informed readiness
rows.statement: Purification redefined as improvement of epistemic quality (clarity up, unsupported claims down, unresolved contradictions down, provenance quality up, discrimination quality up) rather than |K_{t+1}| > |K_t|, respecting the 'more knowledge' != 'more statements' formal ordering problem. The ultimate KnowledgeOS objective is reframed away from 'know everything' or 'make decisions for humans' toward maintaining epistemic readiness: uncertainty -> observation -> understanding -> discrimination -> qualification -> informed readiness.

rows.anchor: Purification is an epistemic transformation that increases the adequacy, coherence, validity and contextual fitness of the knowledge state ... Purification != |K| up ... Purification = Dimension enrichment + Quality improvement + Contradiction reduction + Contextual adequacy ... Sigma_t \preceq \Sigma_{t+1} ... the individual axis orders still require declaration ... Sigma_t \preceq_P \Sigma_{t+1} under a declared purification relation P.
rows.statement: Refines purification mathematically: not |K| increasing but Purification = Dimension enrichment + Quality improvement + Contradiction reduction + Contextual adequacy. Connects to Step 287: rather than a simple total order K_{t+1}>K_t, purification is a partial order Sigma_t preceq Sigma_{t+1} componentwise only where component order is defined, i.e. Sigma_t preceq_P Sigma_{t+1} under a declared purification relation P -- preserving Step 287's warning that a product partial order is plausible but individual axis orders still require declaration.

lineage_claims.target: prior formulation 'purification means increasing the dimension of knowledge as well as the value towards each dimension'
lineage_claims.quote: I would refine your earlier formulation.

rows.anchor: Purification transformation P: K_t -> K_{t+1} ... P(K_t) = reduce contradiction + increase justification + improve provenance + resolve ambiguity + correct relations + remove unsupported propositions ... Purification != Accumulation. Rather: Purification = epistemic transformation.
rows.statement: Purification formalized as a transformation P: K_t -> K_{t+1} where P(K_t) = reduce contradiction + increase justification + improve provenance + resolve ambiguity + correct relations + remove unsupported propositions -- rejecting |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| as the definition; Purification != Accumulation, Purification = epistemic transformation.

rows.anchor: We should NOT impose 'knowledge can only increase' ... We should not assume K_t subseteq K_{t+1} for every operation. Instead: K_{t+1} = op(K_t,x) and the operator declares its transformation law. ... Add, Revise, Retract, Qualify, Relate, Observe, Act ... Each has different algebraic properties.
rows.statement: Rejects imposing K_t subseteq K_{t+1} (knowledge-can-only-increase) as a universal law -- particularly important for the purification theory; instead each operator (Add, Revise, Retract, Qualify, Relate, Observe, Act) declares its own transformation law with its own algebraic properties, K_{t+1}=op(K_t,x).

rows.anchor: purification operator P: K_t -> K_{t+1} such that selected epistemic quality measures improve ... Q(K)=(q_1,...,q_n) ... Q(K_{t+1}) succeq Q(K_t) for specified dimensions. But we must not invent these dimensions yet. ... Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) ... Step 287 correctly warned us that the per-axis orders are not all established. So we cannot yet claim Sigma_t preceq Sigma_{t+1} universally.
rows.statement: Defines the purification operator P: K_t -> K_{t+1} as requiring improvement of a to-be-defined quality vector Q(K)=(q_1,...,q_n), Q(K_{t+1}) succeq Q(K_t) for specified dimensions -- explicitly warning not to invent these dimensions yet. Connects to the five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C), P: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1}, but reaffirms Step 287's warning that per-axis orders are not all established, so Sigma_t preceq Sigma_{t+1} cannot yet be claimed universally.

rows.anchor: Phi(K_t) represent the epistemic quality/fitness of the state. Purification: K_t -P-> K_{t+1} such that Phi(K_{t+1}) succcurlyeq Phi(K_t) for the relevant dimensions. But Phi itself must be defined. ... K_t -> K_t + 100 unsupported claims increases information quantity but decreases epistemic quality. Knowledge growth != Knowledge purification.
rows.statement: Defines an epistemic quality/fitness function Phi(K_t) and purification as K_t --P--> K_{t+1} such that Phi(K_{t+1}) succeq Phi(K_t) on the relevant dimensions, explicitly noting Phi itself is undefined and must not be assumed to increase with state size -- illustrated by K_t -> K_t+100 unsupported claims, which increases information quantity while decreasing epistemic quality: Knowledge growth != Knowledge purification.

rows.anchor: SD-8 Purification operators: P: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1} where purification could mean Delta Dim(Sigma) >= 0 and/or Delta Value(Sigma) >= 0. But there is a major mathematical issue: not every dimension necessarily has an ordering. ... an ordering for S might be possible, while A may not naturally have one. Therefore purification cannot simply mean Sigma_{t+1} > Sigma_t until each axis has a declared order.
rows.statement: SD-8 Purification operators formalized as P: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1} where purification could mean Delta Dim(Sigma)>=0 and/or Delta Value(Sigma)>=0, explicitly flagged a research hypothesis, not a canonical definition, since not every Sigma axis necessarily has an ordering (S may order, A may not per Step 287) -- purification cannot mean Sigma_{t+1}>Sigma_t until each axis has a declared order, an explicit Tactical Discovery task.

rows.anchor: Purification is not currently an order-theoretic operator. Because Sigma exists as a candidate measurement space but Sigma's component orders are not established and Sigma-order does not imply K-order. Therefore Purification = research hypothesis, not P: Sigma -> Sigma as a canonical mathematical operator.
rows.statement: Strengthens the correction on purification: given Sigma's component orders are not established and Sigma-order does not imply K-order, Purification is not currently an order-theoretic operator at all -- it must be recorded as Purification = research hypothesis, not as a canonical mathematical operator P: Sigma -> Sigma.

lineage_claims.target: S2273's purification operator P: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1}
lineage_claims.quote: Given the Step-287/288 discoveries, I would explicitly state: Purification is not currently an order-theoretic operator.

rows.anchor: I would not keep P: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1} as a formal operator. The correct current formulation is: Purification = hypothesis about desirable trajectories of epistemic state ... We cannot define 'toward Moksha' mathematically until we know what ordering 'better knowledge' means. And Step 287/288 has taught us exactly this lesson: an ordering requires a decision procedure.
rows.statement: Further corrects purification: not a formal operator P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1}, but a hypothesis about desirable trajectories of epistemic state (candidate: Dim(Sigma_{t+1})>=Dim(Sigma_t) and/or Value_i(t+1)>=Value_i(t), neither canonical); 'toward Moksha' cannot be defined mathematically until an ordering for 'better knowledge' is established, per Step 287/288's lesson that an ordering requires a decision procedure.

rows.anchor: Purification: Sigma_t -> Sigma_{t+1} is premature. The research explicitly classifies purification as unresolved because the ordering of Sigma has not been established. Instead: Purification = a hypothesis about the quality of a trajectory. So a transformation can be K_t -> K_{t+1} without automatically being K_t prec K_{t+1} and certainly without automatically being K_t -> Moksha.
rows.statement: Further reinforces the purification correction: Purification: Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} is premature since Sigma's ordering is unestablished; Purification = a hypothesis about the quality of a trajectory, so a transformation K_t->K_{t+1} need not be K_t prec K_{t+1}, and certainly need not be K_t -> Moksha.

rows.anchor: So 'purification' can no longer simply mean Value_i up. It may also mean dim(D_t) up, because a richer understanding can reveal dimensions that were previously invisible.
rows.statement: Extends the purification concept: it can no longer mean only Value_i increasing, but may also mean dim(D_t) increasing, since a richer understanding can reveal previously invisible dimensions -- an explicit expansion of the purification concept beyond value-improvement to dimension-discovery.

rows.anchor: P(K_t) which might depend on f(dimension coverage, value quality, epistemic certainty, consistency, evidence, relevance, coherence). Then purification would mean P(K_{t+1})>P(K_t) if we can mathematically define a valid partial order or scalar/vector quality measure. That is exactly where our earlier Sigma_t idea should return -- but only after we determine its mathematical structure.
rows.statement: Proposes a future candidate purification functional P(K_t) = f(dimension coverage, value quality, epistemic certainty, consistency, evidence, relevance, coherence) -- a seven-factor function -- with purification meaning P(K_{t+1})>P(K_t) only if a valid partial order or scalar/vector quality measure can be mathematically defined; notes this is where the earlier Sigma_t construct should return, but only after its mathematical structure is determined.

rows.anchor: Do not assume Purification=more dimensions and do not assume Purification=higher values. Instead investigate a possible quality functional P(K_t) or vector-valued quality Sigma(K_t) and determine whether a meaningful ordering K_a preceq K_b exists. Possible factors: coverage, evidence, consistency, accuracy, relevance, coherence, uncertainty reduction, structural completeness, explanatory power. Do not combine these into one scalar unless mathematically justified. A partial order may be more appropriate than a total order.
rows.statement: Forbids two default purification definitions (more dimensions; higher values), instead requiring investigation of a quality functional P(K_t) or vector Sigma(K_t) and whether a meaningful ordering K_a preceq K_b exists, over nine candidate quality factors (coverage, evidence, consistency, accuracy, relevance, coherence, uncertainty reduction, structural completeness, explanatory power) -- explicitly warning against combining them into one scalar unless mathematically justified, and suggesting a partial order may be more appropriate than a total order.

rows.anchor: Purification = f(coverage, connectivity, coherence, evidence, uncertainty, boundary clarity, value quality). More dimensions != better knowledge. More connectivity != better knowledge. A false relationship can make a knowledge graph more connected while making the knowledge worse. This is where Buddhi + Zero + evidence become essential. ... Purification -> increasing structural coherence of the knowledge space. Potential candidates for coherence: fewer contradictions, fewer unsupported connections, better evidence connectivity, clearer boundaries, reduced uncertainty, stable equivalence classes, improved explanatory relationships. This is something we should investigate mathematically rather than assume.
rows.statement: Extends purification to a seven-factor function including topological terms: Purification = f(coverage, connectivity, coherence, evidence, uncertainty, boundary clarity, value quality), with explicit warnings that more dimensions and more connectivity each do NOT imply better knowledge (a false relationship can increase connectivity while worsening knowledge -- requiring Buddhi+Zero+evidence to guard against this). Proposes a sharper hypothesis: purification -> increasing structural coherence, with seven candidate coherence measures (fewer contradictions, fewer unsupported connections, better evidence connectivity, clearer boundaries, reduced uncertainty, stable equivalence classes, improved explanatory relationships), to be investigated mathematically, not assumed.

rows.anchor: We repeatedly want to say K_1 < K_2 or K_2 is more purified than K_1, but we have not defined <. We may need K_1 preceq K_2 as a partial order rather than a numerical ranking, meaning K_2 contains no epistemic degradation relative to K_1 and improves at least one dimension. But this is only a hypothesis. ... Can knowledge become 'more pure' while losing dimensions? I believe the answer may be yes. Removing irrelevant or false dimensions could represent improvement: dim(K_{t+1})<dim(K_t) while K_t prec K_{t+1}. This would be a very important result.
rows.statement: Flags Knowledge ordering as undefined (K_1<K_2 has no formal meaning), proposing a candidate partial order K_1 preceq K_2 meaning no epistemic degradation plus improvement in at least one dimension -- only a hypothesis. Poses a striking candidate result: purification might involve dimension LOSS (dim(K_{t+1})<dim(K_t) while K_t prec K_{t+1}), since removing irrelevant or false dimensions could itself be an improvement -- a notable inversion of the batch's earlier dimension-expansion-as-purification framing (S2284), flagged as potentially very important if confirmed.

rows.anchor: Purification could mean K_t prec K_{t+1} under a formally defined epistemic ordering. But we should allow dim(K_{t+1})<dim(K_t) while still having K_t prec K_{t+1}. For example, eliminating ten false dimensions could be more valuable than discovering one new true dimension. That is a much stronger theory than more information = more knowledge.
rows.statement: Reinforces (independently of S2294) the dimension-loss-as-purification hypothesis: purification could mean K_t prec K_{t+1} under a formal epistemic ordering while dim(K_{t+1})<dim(K_t), illustrated by 'eliminating ten false dimensions could be more valuable than discovering one new true dimension' -- explicitly a stronger theory than 'more information = more knowledge.'

rows.anchor: H(P_{t+1})<H(P_t). But purification cannot simply be lower entropy. Because a confidently wrong model can have low entropy. Therefore purification should probably involve at least: Evidence quality + consistency + uncertainty + structural coherence. This could lead to a purification functional Phi(P_t,E_t,D_t,tau_t) which we eventually need to define.
rows.statement: Restates the entropy-reduction hazard (a confidently wrong model has low entropy, so purification cannot mean lower entropy alone) and combines it with the topological/statistical strands from prior files into a single candidate purification functional Phi(P_t,E_t,D_t,tau_t) depending on evidence quality, consistency, uncertainty, and structural coherence together -- still to be defined.

rows.anchor: Purification could potentially be a trajectory in a structured Knowledge Space, K_0->K_1->K_2->... with some ordering or functional Phi(K_t) such that Phi(K_{t+1})>=Phi(K_t). But Phi does not necessarily mean amount of knowledge. It could be a multidimensional epistemic quality functional: Phi(K)=f(evidence,consistency,provenance,uncertainty,coherence,dimension,value). This is exactly where our statistical + mathematical + Gītā + DDD research can eventually converge.
rows.statement: Refines purification once more within the layered model: a trajectory K_0->K_1->...->K_t with a functional Phi(K_t) satisfying Phi(K_{t+1})>=Phi(K_t), explicitly not meaning 'amount of knowledge' but a seven-factor multidimensional quality functional Phi(K)=f(evidence,consistency,provenance,uncertainty,coherence,dimension,value) -- framed as the convergence point of the statistical, mathematical, Gita, and DDD research strands.

lexical.anchor: Purification = Dimension Expansion + Dimension Refinement

formal.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t

governance.anchor: Sentence \neq \text{Proposition} \neq \text{Dimension}

rationale_evidence.anchor: E\circ Q \neq Q\circ E ... This is potentially a non-commutative epistemic algebra.
rationale_evidence.statement: Buddhi reframed as an operator-selection mechanism B(K_t,O_t)->which transformation (from {E,R,C,X,Q,Z,...}) is appropriate, rather than another knowledge dimension -- 'the Kernel is not merely storing knowledge, it continuously discriminates what epistemic operation should happen next'. Yoga reframed as operator composition Y = O_n o ... o O_1, e.g. Y_purify = Q o C o R o E o Z (detect absence -> discover dimension -> refine/correct -> qualify -> new state) vs Y_conflict = Q o X o C. Proposes studying the resulting algebra's closure, associativity, and (expected) non-commutativity, e.g. E o Q != Q o E because discovering a dimension before qualification differs from qualifying before discovering it -- hypothesized as a non-commutative epistemic algebra.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \text{Sentence addition} \rightarrow \begin{cases}\text{new dimension}\\\text{new value}\\\text{new context}\\\text{new relation}\\\text{correction}\\\text{qualification}\end{cases}
rationale_evidence.statement: Reframes the purification model: adding a new sentence's important effect is often D_1>D_0 (a new dimension is discovered) rather than |K_1|>|K_0| (more propositions), and further evidence can separately improve the value of an existing dimension v_0(d)->v_1(d); yields a small operator taxonomy that sentence addition maps to: new dimension, new value, new context, new relation, correction, or qualification -- described as exactly the operator algebra sought.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge quantity \neq Knowledge quality ... Purification \neq accumulation
rationale_evidence.statement: Refines purification: P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} must not assume P(Sigma_t)>Sigma_t (per Step 287's finding that axes lack fully declared orders); instead a desired property Q(Sigma_{t+1})>=Q(Sigma_t) is wanted where Q is a future epistemic-quality functional that does not yet exist (an important research gap). Illustrates via example that K_1={1000 unsupported claims} could contain more information than K_2={100 well-supported claims} yet K_2 may be epistemically superior -- so Knowledge quantity != Knowledge quality, and Purification != accumulation; the kernel should maximize epistemic adequacy, not raw knowledge.

assumption_register.statement: the five Sigma axes and Z, U can be meaningfully combined via a weighted linear scalarization
assumption_register.anchor: we should not yet adopt this equation because the measurement scales and ordering of the five axes remain unresolved.

sources.note: Step 231 (tail, phase_measure_theory): poses the unresolved foundational question 'What is K?' and proposes six competing candidate mathematical representations of a knowledge state (Set, Graph, Probabilistic, Typed-proposition, Lattice/ordered, Hybrid), asking for the smallest structure capable of representing knowledge/uncertainty/context/provenance/contradiction/change/verification without collapsing their distinct meanings, without selecting sophistication for its own sake.

rows.anchor: Model A -- Set model K\subseteq X. ... Model F -- Hybrid model K=(Graph, Types, Propositions, Evidence, Probability, Time). We should not select the most mathematically sophisticated model merely because it is sophisticated.
rows.statement: Step 231 (tail) poses 'what is K?' and lists six competing candidate representations of a knowledge state: A) Set model K subseteq X, B) Graph model K=(V,E), C) Probabilistic model K~P_theta, D) Typed proposition model K={(q,s,e,c,t)}, E) Lattice/ordered model K1<=K2, F) Hybrid model K=(Graph,Types,Propositions,Evidence,Probability,Time); explicitly warns against selecting the most sophisticated model merely for its sophistication, and poses the key question of the smallest structure able to represent knowledge/uncertainty/context/provenance/contradiction/change/verification without collapsing their distinct meanings.

rows.anchor: K=everything the system knows. This is unusable. ... would contradict the epistemic distinctions we established in Steps 228-230.
rows.statement: Explicit rejection of the naive starting definition K='everything the system knows', which mixes observations, documents, claims, hypotheses, decisions, rules, code, architecture, evidence, interpretations and AI output into an undifferentiated repository, contradicting the epistemic distinctions established in Steps 228-230.

rows.anchor: k=(q,s,c,t,\sigma,\lambda) where q=proposition, s=epistemic status, c=context, t=temporal validity, \sigma=support/evidence, \lambda=lineage.
rows.statement: A knowledge assertion is formalized as the 6-tuple k=(q,s,c,t,sigma,lambda): proposition/content, epistemic status, context, temporal validity, support/evidence, lineage -- substantially better than k=q alone.

rows.anchor: S=\{Observed,Reported,Inferred,Proposed,Validated,Accepted,Superseded,Rejected\}. Content\neq EpistemicStatus.
rows.statement: Epistemic status s in a provisional 8-value set S={Observed,Reported,Inferred,Proposed,Validated,Accepted,Superseded,Rejected}, with the architectural property Content != EpistemicStatus -- the same proposition can move through several states, e.g. Proposed->Validated->Accepted->Superseded.

rows.anchor: \delta:S\times Event\rightarrow S. ... \delta(Proposed,ValidationPassed)=Validated.
rows.statement: Epistemic status forms a state-transition system: delta:S x Event -> S, e.g. delta(Proposed,ValidationPassed)=Validated -- already implementable and testable, and DDD-interpretable as a KnowledgeItem domain object whose lifecycle (Identity, Proposition, Context, EpistemicStatus, Validity, EvidenceReferences, Lineage) matters, with the invariant 'a material epistemic state transition must be represented'.

rows.anchor: K\subseteq X. ... Set model alone is insufficient. ... G_K=(V,E). ... Graph model is necessary in many cases, but not sufficient. ... K\sim P_\theta. ... Knowledge\neq ProbabilityDistribution.
rows.statement: Systematic elimination of single-structure candidate models for K: Set model (K subseteq X) captures membership but loses ordering/provenance/contradiction/uncertainty/history; Graph model (G_K=(V,E)) captures relationships naturally but not uncertainty/epistemic-status/temporal validity/probability; Probabilistic model (K~P_theta) is useful for uncertain phenomena but most architecture statements (e.g. 'Class X extends Y') are deterministic structural facts, not distributions -- Knowledge != ProbabilityDistribution; probability is a property of some knowledge, not its universal representation.

rows.anchor: K=(V,E,\tau,\pi) where V=typed knowledge nodes, E=typed relationships, \tau=type function, \pi=epistemic/provenance metadata.
rows.statement: Typed proposition model combined with a graph gives K=(V,E,tau,pi): typed knowledge nodes, typed relationships (e.g. tau(v)=Requirement, edge=(v1,supports,v2)), a type function, and epistemic/provenance metadata; worked example Requirement -motivates-> ArchitectureDecision <-supports- TestEvidence illustrates it is far more expressive than a document repository.

rows.anchor: A_1\xleftrightarrow{contradicts}A_2. Then governance can determine what happens. ... Contradiction\neq SystemFailure.
rows.statement: Contradiction must be representable as a first-class relation (A1 <-contradicts-> A2) before classical truth resolution is forced, and governance then determines the outcome; Contradiction != SystemFailure -- conflicting claims may differ by context, time, superseding, assumptions, error, or genuine domain uncertainty, making contradiction often an epistemic state requiring resolution rather than a bug.

rows.anchor: \llbracket q_A\rrbracket_{C_A} and \llbracket q_B\rrbracket_{C_B}. This is precisely where bounded contexts become mathematically significant.
rows.statement: Context resolves many apparent contradictions: q_A valid in C_A and q_B valid in C_B with q_A != q_B does not necessarily imply inconsistency once evaluated via their context-relative denotations [[q_A]]_CA and [[q_B]]_CB -- the point at which bounded contexts become mathematically significant.

rows.anchor: False\neq Superseded. ... Validity(k)=[t_{start},t_{end}). Current(k,t)\iff t\in Validity(k).
rows.statement: Temporal knowledge: False != Superseded (a superseded proposition q_2025 is not necessarily false, merely no longer current), formalized via Validity(k)=[t_start,t_end) and Current(k,t) iff t in Validity(k) -- giving temporal semantics to knowledge.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1}=T(K_t,C,E,A,P). ... T_t:(K_t,C_t,E_t,A_t,P_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1}.
rows.statement: The knowledge state is dynamic: rather than a static K, K_t evolves via a governed transformation T_t:(K_t,C_t,E_t,A_t,P_t)->K_{t+1}, becoming the central state-transition equation connecting directly to the transformation-centric architecture.

rows.anchor: K_t=(G_t,\Sigma_t,\Theta_t,\Lambda_t). ... K_t=(G_t,\Sigma_t,\Theta_t,\Lambda_t,\Pi_t). ... KnowledgeOS should not force knowledge into one mathematical datatype.
rows.statement: The knowledge state is defined as a hybrid mathematical structure, first as a 4-tuple K_t=(G_t semantic graph, Sigma_t epistemic assignments, Theta_t temporal validity structure, Lambda_t provenance/lineage) then extended to 5 layers with Pi_t (probabilistic/uncertainty information): no single conventional mathematical object (graph, logic, time, probability, provenance) alone captures all required dimensions.

rows.anchor: G_t=(V_t,E_t) ... \tau_V, \tau_E ... motivates, supports, contradicts, refines, implements, supersedes.
rows.statement: Layer 1 (Semantic graph): G_t=(V_t,E_t) with node-type function tau_V and relation-type function tau_E over named relation types {motivates, supports, contradicts, refines, implements, supersedes}.

rows.anchor: \sigma:V_t\rightarrow S. ... This prevents content and status from being conflated.
rows.statement: Layer 2 (Epistemic state): sigma:V_t -> S assigns each node an epistemic status (e.g. Accepted, Proposed), preventing content and status conflation.

rows.anchor: \theta:V_t\rightarrow TimeIntervals. ... historically valid from currently valid.
rows.statement: Layer 3 (Temporal validity): theta:V_t -> TimeIntervals (e.g. theta(v)=[2026-01-01,2026-07-01)) distinguishes historically valid from currently valid.

rows.anchor: \lambda(v) as a provenance subgraph. Requirement\leftarrow Meeting\leftarrow Observation\leftarrow Source.
rows.statement: Layer 4 (Provenance): lambda(v) is a provenance subgraph (e.g. Requirement<-Meeting<-Observation<-Source) reconstructing why a knowledge item exists.

rows.anchor: \pi(v) can represent uncertainty. ... The architecture must not force all uncertainty into a number.
rows.statement: Layer 5 (Uncertainty): pi(v) may represent a probability, confidence interval, likelihood, or qualitative uncertainty category -- explicitly must not force all uncertainty into a single number.

rows.anchor: Number\neq Probability. Confidence\neq Truth. KnowledgeOS should carry the semantics of the uncertainty measure.
rows.statement: Important statistical principle: a confidence score like 0.83 is meaningless without defining what it means (model probability? expert confidence? empirical accuracy? posterior? heuristic ranking?) -- Number != Probability and Confidence != Truth; the uncertainty measure's semantics must be carried explicitly.

rows.anchor: \mathfrak K_t=(G_t,\sigma_t,\theta_t,\lambda_t,\pi_t) as the candidate mathematical representation of a knowledge state. ... It is a candidate Knowledge State Algebra.
rows.statement: The candidate mathematical knowledge-state object is finalized as mathfrak K_t=(G_t,sigma_t,theta_t,lambda_t,pi_t), explicitly named a candidate Knowledge State Algebra (not yet a final theorem), with transformation T_t: mathfrak K_t x C_t x E_t x A_t x P_t -> mathfrak K_{t+1} as the most complete formulation so far.

rows.anchor: \Delta_t=(\Delta_t^+,\Delta_t^-,\Delta_t^\sim).
rows.statement: Transformation delta is decomposed rather than treated as naive graph subtraction: Delta_t = (Delta_t^+ additions, Delta_t^- removals, Delta_t^~ modifications) -- a much better representation of change.

rows.anchor: m_C(\Delta)\in\{0,1\}. MaterialChange=m_C(\Delta)=1.
rows.statement: Materiality function m_C(Delta) in {0,1} determines whether a change is material in context C, giving MaterialChange = m_C(Delta)=1 -- a formal bridge between domain semantics and transformation governance.

rows.anchor: if m_C(\Delta_t)=1, then GovernanceRecord(T_t)\neq\varnothing.
rows.statement: The central invariant made precise: for every transformation T_t, if m_C(Delta_t)=1 (material change), then GovernanceRecord(T_t) must be non-empty; cross-context transformations additionally require semantic-impact evaluation.

rows.anchor: \mathcal M_{C_A}(\mathfrak K_A) must be mapped explicitly into \mathcal M_{C_B}(\mathfrak K_B) or identified as intentionally lost. UnmappedMaterialMeaning\Rightarrow TransformationViolation.
rows.statement: Semantic preservation function M_C(mathfrak K) gives the set of material semantic distinctions in context C; crossing contexts, M_{CA}(K_A) must be explicitly mapped into M_{CB}(K_B) or identified as intentionally lost, giving UnmappedMaterialMeaning => TransformationViolation.

rows.anchor: A bounded context protects M_C. A context mapping defines phi_AB. A transformation executes T. Governance authorizes A. Evidence supports E. Lineage records lambda. ... the mathematical model and DDD model are now aligned.
rows.statement: DDD-mathematics alignment table: bounded context protects M_C, context mapping defines phi_AB, transformation executes T, governance authorizes A, evidence supports E, lineage records lambda -- diagrammed as a candidate KnowledgeOS meta-model with Context above a Transformation node fed by Evidence and Authority and producing Knowledge K (Graph/Epistemics/Time/Provenance/Uncertainty).

rows.anchor: Rejected A: K=documents. ... Rejected D: K=P(X). Too probabilistic. ... Rejected E: K=graph only.
rows.statement: Five candidate formulations of K are explicitly and provisionally rejected: documents (too narrow), database records (implementation-centric), all information (semantically undefined), a probability distribution P(X) (too probabilistic), graph only (cannot adequately represent epistemic/temporal state) -- narrowing to the preferred hybrid mathfrak K_t=(G_t,sigma_t,theta_t,lambda_t,pi_t), explicitly labeled the working, not final, mathematical kernel.

rows.anchor: It should be introduced only where the engineering problem genuinely requires it. ... Use the weakest mathematical structure that faithfully represents the phenomenon.
rows.statement: Distribution theory (including generalized functions/distributions T in D' acting on test functions via <T,phi>) is placed correctly at the uncertainty/observation layer only, never as the definition of the entire knowledge object, governed by the statistical architecture principle: use the weakest mathematical structure that faithfully represents the phenomenon -- Logic for deterministic architecture, GraphTheory for relational knowledge, Probability/Statistics for uncertainty, TemporalModels for change, FormalSemantics/DDD for semantics, ProvenanceGraphs for lineage.

rows.anchor: MathematicalKernel\rightarrow DomainArchitecture\rightarrow SoftwareImplementation and separately PhilosophicalInterpretation\leftrightarrow ArchitecturalMeaning. ... we must never write Gita\Rightarrow\mathfrak K_t.
rows.statement: Relation to the Gita restated at the mathematical-kernel level: the Gita stays outside the formal definition, in a separate track (MathematicalKernel->DomainArchitecture->SoftwareImplementation) alongside (PhilosophicalInterpretation<->ArchitecturalMeaning); explicitly forbidding Gita=>mathfrak K_t as an unjustified causal claim -- the defensible relationship is that the Gita offers an interpretive lens for some architectural questions.

rows.anchor: \mathfrak K_t=(G_t,\sigma_t,\theta_t,\lambda_t,\pi_t) ... This is the most promising mathematical foundation so far.
rows.statement: Step 231 conclusion: K is neither merely a set, graph, nor probability distribution; the strongest current model is mathfrak K_t=(G_t semantic structure, sigma_t epistemic status, theta_t temporal validity, lambda_t provenance, pi_t uncertainty where applicable), with mathfrak K_{t+1}=T(mathfrak K_t,C,E,A,P) -- rated the most promising mathematical foundation so far.

rows.anchor: Y=natively representable, P=representable only with an added construction, N=not representable. ... | assertions | Y | Y | P | Y | N | Y |
rows.statement: Executed 17-capability x 6-model capability matrix (Y/P/N scale) testing Step 231's six candidate K models (A Set, B Graph, C Probabilistic, D Typed-proposition, E Lattice, F Hybrid) against assertions/evidence/provenance/context/contradiction/uncertainty/temporal-evolution/supersession/authority/validation/unknown/missingness/non-identifiability/governance/lineage/replay/state-transition, yielding scores (Y+0.5P): A=4.0, B=10.0, C=6.0, D=12.0, E=5.0, F=14.5.

rows.anchor: authority A:N B:P C:N D:P E:N ... K should NOT carry authority, validation, governance or replay. Every attempt to make a single structure represent them forces a P.
rows.statement: Principal result: four capabilities (authority, validation, governance, replay) are natively representable (Y) by NO model at all, including the hybrid Model F which scores only P on all four -- interpreted not as a model deficiency but as evidence these four are not properties of a knowledge state at all: Authority is a relation between actor and action (a property of a transformation, not a state), Validation is an external assessment of a state (a state cannot validate itself without circularity), Governance is a relation between policy and transformation, and Replay is a property of a history of transformations, not any single state.

rows.anchor: This vindicates the kernel's shape while refuting Model F. \mathcal K=(K,C,T,E,A) is right to keep A separate from K -- and Model F is wrong to try to absorb everything into K.
rows.statement: The four-capability result vindicates Step 230's kernel decision to keep Authority A separate from K while directly refuting Step 231's own preferred hybrid Model F for trying to absorb authority (among other things) into K -- Steps 230 and 231's proposals are shown to be in unnoticed tension, and the matrix independently confirms the mandate's own hint that the correct answer may be a typed family of related structures rather than one tuple.

rows.anchor: K = {(q,s,e,c,t,u)} ... with authority, validation, governance and replay held OUTSIDE K -- in A, in assessment operations, in Policy, and in History(T) respectively. Status: VERIFIER RECOMMENDS / PROPOSED RECONSTRUCTION.
rows.statement: Model D (typed proposition tuples K={(q,s,e,c,t)}) is the executed-matrix-strongest single structure (8 Y's, only 1 N: non-identifiability); the derived (not corpus-established) recommendation augments it with an uncertainty annotation u to cover that gap: K={(q,s,e,c,t,u)}, with authority/validation/governance/replay explicitly held outside K -- a refinement of, not an invention beyond, the corpus's own Model D candidate, explicitly flagged VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not CORPUS ESTABLISHES.

rows.anchor: A REFUTED as adequate ... B PARTIALLY ADEQUATE ... C REFUTED as a general model; NECESSARY as a component ... D STRONGEST SINGLE MODEL ... E REFUTED as adequate ... F UNDER-SPECIFIED.
rows.statement: Model-by-model verdicts: A (bare set) refuted as adequate, carrying no provenance/context/uncertainty/evidence; B (graph) partially adequate, strong on relational concerns but cannot express uncertainty or non-identifiability; C (probabilistic) refuted as a general model yet necessary as a component (only model natively handling uncertainty AND non-identifiability); D (typed propositions) strongest single model; E (lattice/order) refuted as adequate, a relation ON knowledge states not a model OF one; F (hybrid) under-specified -- scores highest only because it is a list of six structures with no integration rule, no stated typing, no interaction semantics, no equality, no membership.

rows.anchor: it re-introduces the E double-binding recorded in KERNEL-AUDIT-230-232.md §7 -- Evidence appears inside K here while also being kernel component E.
rows.statement: Model F (the corpus's own preferred candidate) is cross-referenced as re-introducing the Evidence double-binding defect already recorded in the separate KERNEL-AUDIT-230-232 report: Evidence appears both inside K (via Model F) and as the separate sibling kernel component E, with no stated distinction.

rows.anchor: K is currently undefined | CORPUS ESTABLISHES ... Model F is the answer | SOURCE CLAIM -- asserted, not argued ... Model D is the strongest single structure | VERIFIED (executed matrix)
rows.statement: Explicit corpus-vs-audit evidence-class table separating what the corpus itself establishes (K is undefined; six candidate models are worth testing) from what is merely a source claim (Model F is the answer, asserted not argued) versus what this audit independently VERIFIES (no model natively carries authority/validation/governance/replay; those four belong outside K; Model D is the strongest single structure) versus what the audit only RECOMMENDS (the augmented K={(q,s,e,c,t,u)} form).

rows.anchor: No integration rule for Model F. Until one exists, F is not a mathematical object. ... K_1=K_2 is never given a criterion, which blocks Replay, Merge and Supersede in Step 232's algebra.
rows.statement: Open issues: Model F has no integration rule and so is not yet a mathematical object; equality and identity on K are undefined in ALL six models (K1=K2 has no criterion anywhere), which blocks Step 232's Replay/Merge/Supersede algebra operations; Model D's status field s has no declared value set, and the corpus carries eleven competing epistemic-status vocabularies (tracked as TV-F-074), so Model D cannot be instantiated until one is chosen.

rows.anchor: BLOCKER 3 -- INTEGRITY ... absent from every late kernel. Step 230-232 dropped a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses. ... BLOCKER 5 -- TRANSITION AT SCALE ... unmeasured.
rows.statement: Blocker 3: integrityHash exists in production code and in Step 073's cryptographic-provenance work but is absent from every late-stage (Step 230-232) kernel formulation -- a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses was dropped. Blocker 5: the kernel only computes on 1-2 items; complexity/behavior at realistic scale is unmeasured. Also notes the ~25 registries, the four E-scales, and the two kernel lineages are NOT theory gaps but documentation/naming issues -- the underlying mathematics is unaffected by how many times it was renamed.

aliases: Step 13: Sufficiency, Completeness, and Readiness for Purpose

sources.note: S0867's Step 13: purpose-relative sufficiency (not universal completeness); three-valued requirement satisfaction with criticality-gated blocking; the Epistemic/Governance/Operational (Sufficient/Authorized/Ready) separation; RiskAcceptance never erases a recorded KnowledgeGap; purpose-relative Ideal State and discrepancy; a policy-predicate (non-scalar) Ready_rho; a ReadinessCertificate audit artifact; S1-S10 invariants; hands off to Step 14 (causality/dependency/counterfactual reasoning).

rows.anchor:
When can KnowledgeOS legitimately say: We know enough to proceed? That is fundamentally different from saying We know everything. ... complete knowledge is generally impossible. ... The correct concept is purpose-relative sufficiency. ... Truth
eq Knowledge
eq Completeness
eq Sufficiency ... Suff
rows.statement: States the governing principle of purpose-relative sufficiency (not universal completeness), separating five concepts: Truth ≠ Knowledge ≠ Completeness ≠ Sufficiency ≠ DecisionReadiness.

rows.anchor: Truth ... Truth(P) ... KnowledgeOS generally cannot directly determine this for arbitrary propositions. It can determine Supported(P) or Accepted(P). Accepted(P)\not\Rightarrow Truth(P). This remains one of our foundational invariants.
rows.statement: Reaffirms Accepted(P) ⇏ Truth(P) as a foundational invariant, since KnowledgeOS cannot generally determine Truth(P) directly for arbitrary propositions.

rows.anchor: Completeness ... K_t=I^K_{P_r} ... this is usually unrealistic. There may always be unknown information; future changes; unmodeled dimensions; irrelevant details. Absolute completeness is generally not required.
rows.statement: Argues absolute completeness (K_t=I^K_{P_r}) is generally unrealistic and not required, given always-possible unknown information, future change, unmodeled dimensions, and irrelevant details.

rows.anchor: Purpose-relative completeness ... \mathcal Q(P_r) containing everything that must be known for purpose P_r. Purpose: migrate Nexus. Q_1=CurrentVersion, Q_2=HostIdentity, Q_3=NetworkDependencies, Q_4=FirewallRules, Q_5=BackupCapability, Q_6=CertificateStatus ... Completeness(K_t,P_r) = coverage of Q(
rows.statement: Defines a purpose-relative requirement set Q(P_r) (illustrated with six Nexus-migration requirements) and Completeness(K_t,P_r) as coverage of that set.

rows.anchor: But coverage is not enough ... all six questions have answers ... BackupStatus=Contested. The knowledge coverage is high, but the state may not be safe enough for migration. Coverage\neq Sufficiency.
rows.statement: Shows full requirement coverage can still be insufficient (e.g. a contested backup status), establishing Coverage ≠ Sufficiency.

rows.anchor: Epistemic sufficiency ... Sufficient_\rho(K_t,P_r) ... The current Knowledge State satisfies the minimum epistemic requirements necessary for purpose P_r, according to policy \rho. Sufficient_\rho = f(Coverage,Support,Uncertainty,Conflict,Validity,Criticality). The function is policy-defined.
rows.statement: Defines Sufficient_ρ(K_t,P_r) as a policy-defined function of Coverage, Support, Uncertainty, Conflict, Validity, and Criticality — not coverage alone.

rows.anchor: Requirement-level evaluation ... q=(Target,Condition,MinimumEpistemicState,Context,Criticality) ... Target = BackupCapability, Condition = RestoreTestSuccessful, MinimumSupport = Strong, Conflict = None, Validity = Current, Criticality = High.
rows.statement: Defines a KnowledgeRequirement q=(Target,Condition,MinimumEpistemicState,Context,Criticality), worked with a BackupCapability/RestoreTestSuccessful example.

rows.anchor: Requirement satisfaction ... Satisfies(K_t,q)\in\{True,False,Unknown\} ... Backup restore test: Unknown does not mean False. Unknown\neq False. This continues our open-world principle.
rows.statement: Defines three-valued Satisfies(K_t,q)∈{True,False,Unknown}, reaffirming Unknown≠False as continuing the open-world principle.

rows.anchor: Three-valued requirement evaluation ... \mathbb T_3=\{Satisfied,Unsatisfied,Unknown\} ... Current version known Satisfied ... Backup restore tested Unknown ... Firewall dependencies known Unsatisfied. Now the overall readiness can be evaluated.
rows.statement: Works a worked requirement table (version/owner Satisfied, backup-restore Unknown, firewall-dependencies Unsatisfied) illustrating T_3={Satisfied,Unsatisfied,Unknown}.

rows.anchor: Critical requirements ... Criticality(q)\in\{Low,Medium,High,Critical\} ... Critical(q)=True \land Satisfies(K,q)\neq Satisfied means NotReady. Thus a single unresolved critical requirement may block an action even when 95% of the knowledge is complete.
rows.statement: Defines Criticality(q) and the rule that any unsatisfied Critical requirement forces NotReady regardless of overall coverage percentage.

rows.anchor: This is why scalar completeness is dangerous ... Coverage=95% ... perhaps the missing 5% is: Does the backup actually restore? Then 95% may still mean NotReady. Percentage completeness cannot replace requirement-level evaluation. A scalar can be useful as a summary, but never as the fundamental deci
rows.statement: Warns a high percentage-completeness score (95%) can still mean NotReady if the missing fraction is the critical requirement — scalar completeness must never replace requirement-level evaluation.

rows.anchor: Sufficiency vector ... \mathbf S(K_t,P_r) = (s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_n) where each s_i=Satisfies(K_t,q_i). This preserves the individual deficiencies. \mathbf S=(1,1,1,0,?,1)
rows.statement: Defines a sufficiency vector S(K_t,P_r)=(s1,...,sn) over per-requirement satisfaction values, preserving individual deficiencies rather than collapsing to a scalar.

rows.anchor: Decision readiness ... Ready_\rho(K_t,P_r) ... This is not purely epistemic. It can depend on epistemic sufficiency; risk; authority; constraints; policy; operational conditions. DecisionReadiness = f(EpistemicSufficiency,Risk,Authority,Constraints,Purpose,Policy).
rows.statement: Defines DecisionReadiness=f(EpistemicSufficiency,Risk,Authority,Constraints,Purpose,Policy) as broader than epistemic sufficiency alone.

rows.anchor: Example ... 92% coverage ... Critical uncertainty: Backup restore test unknown ... Risk: High ... Authority: Architecture Board ... Policy: Migration requires verified recovery ... Sufficient=False and Ready=False. Lord should propose: Perform restore test. Sārathi should recommend: Do not proceed u
rows.statement: Worked migration-readiness example (92% coverage, critical uncertainty, high risk) producing Sufficient=False and Ready=False, with Lord/Sārathi recommending the restore test before proceeding.

rows.anchor: But sometimes action is allowed despite uncertainty ... Criticality=Medium ... the business accepts the risk. Then Sufficient=False but Ready=True may still be possible if AcceptRisk=True. Epistemic insufficiency does not always imply operational prohibition. Instead the organization may explicitly
rows.statement: Shows Sufficient=False can still coexist with Ready=True given explicit risk acceptance at Medium criticality — epistemic insufficiency does not always imply operational prohibition.

rows.anchor: This creates a crucial separation ... Epistemic decision Do we know enough? Sufficient? ... Governance decision Are we authorized to proceed despite the remaining gap? Authorized? ... Operational decision Should we execute? Ready? ... Sufficient\neq Authorized\neq Ready. This is an extremely importa
rows.statement: Draws a three-way DDD boundary between Epistemic (Sufficient?), Governance (Authorized?), and Operational (Ready?) decisions — Sufficient ≠ Authorized ≠ Ready.

rows.anchor: Risk acceptance ... q_4=Unknown. But an authorized body explicitly accepts the risk: RiskAccepted(q_4). Then Ready may become true. But KnowledgeOS must retain q_4=Unknown. It must never transform RiskAccepted into Known. RiskAcceptance does not eliminate epistemic uncertainty.
rows.statement: Requires RiskAcceptance never eliminate the underlying epistemic uncertainty: an accepted-risk requirement remains recorded Unknown even when Ready becomes True — RiskAcceptance does not eliminate epistemic uncertainty.

rows.anchor: This gives us a powerful distinction ... The Architecture Board says: Proceed anyway; risk accepted. KnowledgeOS should record KnowledgeGap=True and RiskAccepted=True. Not KnowledgeGap=False. This is exactly the kind of distinction an enterprise knowledge system needs.
rows.statement: Illustrates recording both KnowledgeGap=True and RiskAccepted=True simultaneously (never collapsing the gap to False) after an authorized risk-accepted proceed decision.

rows.anchor: Ideal State revisited ... Relevant_\rho(d,P_r) ... \Delta_t^{P_r} = \{d\in\Delta_t\mid Relevant_\rho(d,P_r)\}. This gives us a purpose-specific discrepancy. ... Purpose-specific Ideal State ... I_t(P_r) ... I_t(Migration) differs from I_t(Audit). ... Completeness becomes purpose-relative ... Complet
rows.statement: Redefines the Ideal State and discrepancy as purpose-relative — I_t(P_r) and Δ_t^{P_r}=Relevant_ρ(d,P_r)-filtered — concluding there is no universal 'complete knowledge', only knowledge sufficient for a specified purpose under specified conditions.

rows.anchor: Readiness as a predicate ... Ready_\rho(K_t,P_r) \iff \forall q\in Q(P_r): RequirementCondition_\rho(K_t,q) with exceptions for explicitly authorized risk acceptance. ... Ready_\rho = Policy_\rho(RequirementStates,RiskAcceptances,Authority,Constraints). ... No universal readiness formula ... Ready=0
rows.statement: Formalizes Ready_ρ as a universally-quantified requirement predicate with risk-acceptance exceptions, generalized to Ready_ρ=Policy_ρ(RequirementStates,RiskAcceptances,Authority,Constraints), explicitly warning against a scalar formula like Ready=0.95×KnowledgeScore as a serious theoretical mistake.

rows.anchor: Safety-critical versus exploratory purposes ... Exploratory research may tolerate Uncertainty=High. Architecture decision may require Uncertainty\leq Moderate. Production deployment may require CriticalUncertainty=None. Thresholds belong to PurposePolicy.
rows.statement: Shows different purposes require different uncertainty thresholds (exploratory tolerates High, architecture decisions Moderate, production None for critical items) — thresholds belong to PurposePolicy.

rows.anchor: This is where Governance enters ... EpistemicPolicy determines How evidence is assessed. AcceptancePolicy determines When a proposition becomes accepted. DecisionPolicy determines When knowledge is sufficient for a particular action. These must not be collapsed.
rows.statement: Names three separate policy layers — EpistemicPolicy, AcceptancePolicy, DecisionPolicy — each governing a distinct question, none to be collapsed into another.

rows.anchor: DDD model ... KnowledgeRequirement ... Purpose ... SufficiencyAssessment ... ReadinessAssessment ... RiskAcceptance ... DecisionAuthority ... This gives us a strong domain model.
rows.statement: Introduces six DDD concepts (KnowledgeRequirement, Purpose, SufficiencyAssessment, ReadinessAssessment, RiskAcceptance, DecisionAuthority) as the domain model for readiness.

rows.anchor: Example domain flow ... Purpose: Migrate Nexus → Knowledge Requirements → Current Knowledge State → Sufficiency Assessment (Sufficient/Insufficient/Unknown) → Risk Assessment → Authority → Decision Readiness. This is much closer to an enterprise-grade knowledge operating system.
rows.statement: Assembles the readiness domain flow: Purpose→KnowledgeRequirements→CurrentKnowledgeState→SufficiencyAssessment→RiskAssessment→Authority→DecisionReadiness.

rows.anchor: Connection to Zero ... K_t against I_t(P). It produces \Delta_t^P. But it can also classify discrepancies: Blocking, Non-blocking, Informational, Unknown, Risk-accepted. ... Connection to Lord ... Lord: \Delta_t^P \rightarrow CandidateActions. The objective is no longer reduce all discrepancy. It is
rows.statement: Extends Zero to classify discrepancies (Blocking/Non-blocking/Informational/Unknown/Risk-accepted), refines Lord to target only purpose-relevant discrepancy (Δ_t^P→CandidateActions), and defines Sārathi as DecisionOrchestration under epistemic and governance constraints.

rows.anchor: Knowledge sufficiency is dynamic ... Ready(K_t,P)=True. Tomorrow Evidence changes. Then Ready(K_{t+1},P) may become False. Readiness has temporal validity. A decision that was justified yesterday may not be justified today.
rows.statement: States Readiness has temporal validity: a Ready determination can flip to False as evidence changes, so a decision justified yesterday may not be justified today.

rows.anchor: Readiness certificate ... ReadinessCertificate ... RC=(Purpose,KnowledgeStateVersion,Requirements,SatisfiedRequirements,OutstandingGaps,RiskAcceptances,Authority,PolicyVersion,Timestamp). This becomes an auditable answer to Why did KnowledgeOS consider this decision ready?
rows.statement: Defines a ReadinessCertificate artifact RC=(Purpose,KnowledgeStateVersion,Requirements,SatisfiedRequirements,OutstandingGaps,RiskAcceptances,Authority,PolicyVersion,Timestamp) as an auditable record answering why a decision was considered ready.

rows.anchor: This is extremely important for deterministic assurance ... Purpose: Nexus Migration, Knowledge State: K-2026-08-27-0042, Requirements: 18, Satisfied: 16, Outstanding: 2, Risk accepted: 2, Authority: Architecture Board, Policy: Migration-Policy v3, Decision: Ready. This is much stronger than "The AI
rows.statement: Worked full ReadinessCertificate example (18 requirements, 16 satisfied, 2 outstanding/risk-accepted, named authority and policy version) contrasted favorably with an unauditable 'the AI said it was okay'.

rows.anchor: Formal model ... Q_P=\{q_1,\ldots,q_n\} ... s_i=Satisfies(K,q_i) ... \mathbf S(K,P) = (s_1,\ldots,s_n) ... RA as authorized risk acceptances ... Ready_\rho(K,P) = DecisionPolicy_\rho(\mathbf S,RA,Authority,Constraints). This is computable for a finite requirement set.
rows.statement: Consolidates the formal readiness model: requirement set Q_P, sufficiency vector S(K,P), authorized risk acceptances RA, and Ready_ρ(K,P)=DecisionPolicy_ρ(S,RA,Authority,Constraints), computable for a finite requirement set.

rows.anchor: Computational viability ... The difficult part is semantic evaluation. But Step 12 already established that arbitrary natural-language equivalence is not always decidable. Therefore a requirement evaluation can itself return Satisfied, Unsatisfied, Unknown. This preserves computability without prete
rows.statement: Notes computational viability of readiness evaluation depends on semantic evaluation, which Step 12 already showed is not always decidable — hence requirement evaluations remain three-valued, preserving computability without pretending omniscience.

rows.anchor:
Step 13 core invariants ... S1 Truth
eq Sufficiency ... S2 Completeness is purpose-relative ... S3 Coverage
eq Sufficiency ... S4 Unknown
eq Unsatisfied ... S5 Sufficient
eq Authorized ... S6 Authorized
eq Ready ... S7 RiskAcceptance does not remove KnowledgeGap ... S8 Readiness is policy-gover
rows.statement: States ten candidate invariants S1-S10: Truth≠Sufficiency, purpose-relative completeness, Coverage≠Sufficiency, Unknown≠Unsatisfied, Sufficient≠Authorized≠Ready, RiskAcceptance doesn't remove KnowledgeGap, policy-governed and temporally-valid readiness, and scalar scores as derived not fundamental.

rows.anchor: Step 13 verdict ... STRUCTURALLY RESOLVED ... KnowledgeOS does not attempt to know everything. It determines whether the available knowledge is sufficient for a defined purpose under a defined policy. This is a much more realistic and computationally defensible objective.
rows.statement: Declares Step 13 structurally resolved with the reframed objective: KnowledgeOS determines whether available knowledge is sufficient for a defined purpose under a defined policy, not whether it knows everything.

rows.anchor: The theory has now reached an important level ... K_t \xrightarrow{Zero} \Delta_t^P \xrightarrow{Lord} CandidateActions \xrightarrow{Sārathi} Action \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow K_{t+1} ... while K_t \rightarrow Sufficiency \rightarrow Readiness \rightarrow Decision runs alongside it. And the hi
rows.statement: Assembles the two parallel loops running alongside each other: the active Zero/Lord/Sārathi acquisition cycle and the Sufficiency→Readiness→Decision evaluation, over the historical foundation K_t=F(K_0,H_t,ρ,Ω).

rows.anchor: Step 14 — the next problem ... How does KnowledgeOS represent causality and dependencies between facts, events, actions, and outcomes? ... BackupConfiguration \rightarrow BackupExecution \rightarrow RestoreTest \rightarrow Recoverability. Or ArchitectureDecision \rightarrow Implementation \rightarro
rows.statement: Poses Step 14: distinguish Correlation ≠ Dependency ≠ Causation ≠ LogicalImplication, illustrated with a backup-recoverability chain and an architecture-decision-to-outcome chain, moving KnowledgeOS from a knowledge repository toward a reasoning/decision system able to answer why/what-caused/what-if questions.
