sources.note: S0863's Step 8: separates Supported/Accepted/Committed/True; defines a non-linear multidimensional acceptance-status space Omega_A; introduces AcceptancePolicy (policy-relative acceptance) and Commitment (purpose/authority-dependent, distinct from Acceptance); Accepted+Contested coexistence; NotAccepted!=Rejected, Unresolved!=Rejected; Accepted !=> IdealSatisfied; A1-A10 candidate constitutional invariants; and the full epistemic pipeline through to Next Acquisition; hands off to Step 9 (contradiction/paraconsistency/belief revision).

rows.anchor:
The central distinction is: Supported 
eq Accepted 
eq Committed 
eq True. This distinction should become one of the core laws of KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: States the governing distinction of Step 8 as a candidate core law of KnowledgeOS: Supported ≠ Accepted ≠ Committed ≠ True.

rows.anchor: The problem ... Strong supporting evidence, No known contradiction, Current, High provenance quality ... Can KnowledgeOS now put P into the Knowledge State as accepted knowledge? Not necessarily. There is a missing concept: AcceptancePolicy. The evidence tells us what the evidence supports. The acce
rows.statement: Argues even strong, uncontradicted, current, high-provenance evidence does not automatically warrant acceptance, introducing AcceptancePolicy as the missing concept determining what may be admitted as accepted knowledge.

rows.anchor: Four epistemic statuses ... Candidate \rightarrow Supported \rightarrow Accepted \rightarrow Committed ... Supported \rightarrow Contested ... Supported \rightarrow Rejected ... Candidate \rightarrow Unresolved ... These are not simply levels of "confidence." They represent different domain states.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Candidate/Supported/Accepted/Committed as a branching progression (not a confidence scale), with additional branches to Contested, Rejected, and Unresolved, insisting these are distinct domain states.

rows.anchor: Candidate ... A proposition becomes a candidate when KnowledgeOS has reason to represent it but does not yet have sufficient basis to accept it. ... LLM extracted from document ... Candidate(P)=True but Accepted(P)=False. This is particularly important for AI-generated knowledge.
rows.statement: Defines Candidate(P) status (proposition represented but not yet accepted), illustrated by an LLM-extracted proposition, flagged as particularly important for AI-generated knowledge.

rows.anchor: Supported ... Supported_\rho(P) = Assessment_\rho(P)\models SupportCondition_\rho ... The evidence provides a defensible basis for the proposition under the selected assessment policy. But Supported(P)\not\Rightarrow Accepted(P).
rows.statement: Defines Supported_ρ(P) as Assessment_ρ(P) satisfying a policy-specific SupportCondition_ρ, explicitly not implying Accepted(P).

rows.anchor: Accepted ... Accept_\rho(P,EA) \rightarrow AcceptedAssertion subject to the acceptance policy. ... One authoritative current source is sufficient ... Two independent observations ... Accepted_{\rho_1}(P)=True while Accepted_{\rho_2}(P)=False. This is not a mathematical contradiction. It is policy de
rows.statement: Defines Accept_ρ(P,EA)→AcceptedAssertion as policy-relative, showing the same evidence can be Accepted under one policy (single authoritative source) and not under another (requiring two independent observations) — policy dependence, not contradiction.

rows.anchor: Commitment ... an organization may accept ... but still not be committed to using that assertion as a basis for an operational decision. "We accept that Nexus is 3.69, but migration approval requires an additional infrastructure verification." Accepted(P)\not\Rightarrow Committed(P). Commitment mean
rows.statement: Defines Commitment as distinct from Acceptance: Accepted(P) ⇏ Committed(P), illustrated by an organization accepting a fact but still requiring additional verification before migration approval; commitment means willingness to rely on the proposition for a defined purpose/action.

rows.anchor: Commitment is purpose-dependent ... Commit_\rho(P,Purpose,Authority) ... Commit(P,migration,ArchitectureBoard) may require more than Commit(P,internal research,Engineer). Commit(P,P_1)\neq Commit(P,P_2). This fits our earlier Ideal State principle: I_t(P_1)\neq I_t(P_2).
rows.statement: Defines Commit_ρ(P,Purpose,Authority) as purpose-dependent, e.g. migration commitment requiring Architecture Board authority versus lighter requirements for internal research, echoing the earlier purpose-dependence of the Ideal State.

rows.anchor: Truth remains outside the state machine ... Accepted(P)\neq True(P) and Committed(P)\neq True(P). KnowledgeOS does not have an oracle for reality. It records what is currently supported, accepted, and/or committed under a defined epistemic and governance regime.
rows.statement: States that neither Accepted(P) nor Committed(P) equals True(P): KnowledgeOS has no oracle for reality, only records what is supported/accepted/committed under a defined regime.

rows.anchor: Formal acceptance function ... \alpha_\rho: EA\times P\times C \rightarrow \mathcal S_A ... \mathcal S_A=\{Candidate,Supported,Accepted,Rejected,Contested,Unresolved\} ... an assertion can be Supported + Contested. So again, we should be careful about a single enum.
rows.statement: Defines α_ρ:EA×P×C→S_A over six statuses, warning against treating S_A as a single mutually-exclusive enum since e.g. Supported+Contested can co-occur.

rows.anchor: Better: acceptance as a multidimensional status ... \Omega_A=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus) ... Support: Strong, Acceptance: Accepted, Commitment: Committed, Contest: Active. This looks strange initially, but it accurately represents real organizational knowledge.
rows.statement: Defines acceptance status as a four-dimensional vector Ω_A=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus), with a worked example showing Accepted+Committed+Contest:Active as coherent, accurately reflecting real organizational knowledge.

rows.anchor: Why "Accepted + Contested" is possible ... an architecture board has formally accepted ... another architect disputes ... Accepted(P)=True while Contested(P)=True. This is not logically impossible. ... The proposition is institutionally accepted while still being epistemically contested. This is exa
rows.statement: Justifies Accepted+Contested coexisting via an architecture-board example (formally accepted decision still disputed by an architect), establishing that epistemic status and governance status must not be collapsed.

rows.anchor: Acceptance policy ... \rho_A = AcceptancePolicy ... Evidence requirements N_{independent}\geq2 ... Source requirements Authority(Source)\geq A_{min} ... Temporal requirements Age(e)\leq T_{max} ... Conflict requirements ActiveConflict(P)=False ... Human approval ... Statistical threshold Pr(P\mid E)
rows.statement: Defines AcceptancePolicy ρ_A as specifying six example condition types (independent-evidence count, source authority minimum, evidence-age maximum, no active conflict, human approval, statistical threshold) — explicitly examples of policy, not universal law.

rows.anchor: This gives us a clean separation ... Mathematics defines what the evidence assessment means. Policy defines when an assessment is sufficient for acceptance. Governance defines who has authority to commit to that knowledge. Assessment \rightarrow AcceptancePolicy \rightarrow Acceptance \rightarrow Go
rows.statement: Draws a three-way separation — mathematics (what assessment means), policy (when acceptance is sufficient), governance (who may commit) — formalized as Assessment→AcceptancePolicy→Acceptance→Governance→Commitment.

rows.anchor: DDD interpretation ... a bounded context around Knowledge Commitment. Assertion ... EvidenceAssessment ... AcceptancePolicy ... AcceptanceDecision ... Commitment ... Authority ... These should not be hidden inside the Assertion entity.
rows.statement: Proposes a Knowledge Commitment bounded context with six concepts (Assertion, EvidenceAssessment, AcceptancePolicy, AcceptanceDecision, Commitment, Authority) that must not be hidden inside the Assertion entity.

rows.anchor: Acceptance is a domain event ... AssertionAccepted should be emitted. AssertionId, AssessmentId, PolicyId, PolicyVersion, Authority, Context, EffectiveFrom, DecisionBasis, Timestamp. This creates an auditable transition.
rows.statement: Defines an AssertionAccepted domain event carrying AssertionId, AssessmentId, PolicyId/Version, Authority, Context, EffectiveFrom, DecisionBasis, Timestamp for auditability.

rows.anchor: Rejection is different from absence of acceptance ... NotAccepted\neq Rejected ... Evidence: insufficient ... The correct state may be Unresolved. It does not mean P=False. Unresolved\neq Rejected. This is critical for incomplete real-world knowledge.
rows.statement: States NotAccepted≠Rejected and Unresolved≠Rejected: insufficient evidence should yield Unresolved, not a claim that P is false — critical for incomplete real-world knowledge.

rows.anchor: Example ... Production Nexus is backed up. ... Infrastructure engineer says yes ... Backup configuration not inspected ... No restore test ... Support: Moderate, Uncertainty: High, Verification: Insufficient ... KnowledgeOS should not conclude \neg P. Nor Accepted(P). The correct result may be Unres
rows.statement: Works a backup-verification example where weak/unverified evidence (engineer's verbal yes, uninspected config, no restore test) correctly yields Unresolved(P) with a Lord recommendation to verify configuration and run a restore test, rather than either Accepted(P) or ¬P.

rows.anchor: Acceptance and Ideal State ... MustBeVerified(BackupStatus) ... Supported(P) may still fail the ideal requirement: \Sigma_K(P)\not\models I^K(P). Accepted(P) \not\Rightarrow IdealSatisfied(P). A proposition can be accepted while the knowledge objective remains incomplete.
rows.statement: Connects Acceptance to the Ideal State: Accepted(P) ⇏ IdealSatisfied(P) — a proposition can be accepted while the underlying knowledge objective (e.g. independent verification) remains incomplete.

rows.anchor: Example ... Nexus = 3.69 Accepted. But the Ideal State requires MustBeKnown, MustBeCurrent, MustBeIndependentlyVerified ... Independent verification = no ... Accepted(P)=True but \Delta_t\neq\emptyset. Acceptance does not mean completion.
rows.statement: Worked example: an accepted Nexus-version assertion still leaves a nonempty discrepancy Δ_t because independent verification is missing — 'Acceptance does not mean completion.'

rows.anchor: This protects us from a major design mistake ... LLM found answer ↓ Answer accepted ↓ Gap closed. Our model rejects that shortcut. Instead: LLM found candidate ↓ Evidence assessment ↓ Acceptance policy ↓ Accepted? ↓ Ideal-state evaluation ↓ Gap closed? These are separate decisions.
rows.statement: Warns against the shortcut 'LLM found answer → gap closed', mandating the full separated pipeline (candidate → assessment → acceptance policy → accepted? → ideal-state evaluation → gap closed?) as distinct decisions.

rows.anchor: Commitment introduces authority ... Committed(P,Migration) may require Authority=ArchitectureBoard. Authority is part of commitment, not evidence. A manager's authority does not make evidence more truthful. It determines what the organization is permitted to commit to.
rows.statement: States Authority is part of commitment, not evidence: an authority figure's approval does not make evidence more truthful, it only determines what the organization is permitted to commit to.

rows.anchor: Human versus AI ... An LLM may produce Candidate(P) ... even Supported(P) if its output is appropriately assessed. But LLMOutput\not\Rightarrow OrganizationalCommitment. A human or governed process may be required. This is an extremely important KnowledgeOS safety property.
rows.statement: States LLMOutput ⇏ OrganizationalCommitment as a KnowledgeOS safety property: an LLM can produce Candidate or even Supported status, but organizational commitment requires a human or governed process.

rows.anchor: Formal state transition ... (EA,P,\rho_A) \rightarrow AcceptanceOutcome ... (AcceptanceOutcome,Authority,Purpose) \rightarrow CommitmentOutcome ... Evidence \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow Acceptance \rightarrow Commitment is formally distinct.
rows.statement: Formalizes (EvidenceAssessment,P,ρ_A)→AcceptanceOutcome and (AcceptanceOutcome,Authority,Purpose)→CommitmentOutcome as two distinct formal transitions.

rows.anchor: Knowledge State integration ... K_t \xrightarrow{AssertionAccepted} K_{t+1} ... K_{t+1} \xrightarrow{CommitmentEstablished} K_{t+2}. But the underlying assertion does not change truth value. Its institutional status changes.
rows.statement: Models acceptance and commitment as two successive Knowledge State transitions (via AssertionAccepted then CommitmentEstablished events) that change institutional status, never the assertion's truth value.

rows.anchor: A useful formal decomposition ... A=(P,\Sigma,\Omega,\Pi,\tau,Ctx) ... \Sigma=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) ... \Omega=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus). Epistemic state ... Governance state ... That separation is extremely important.
rows.statement: Decomposes an assertion as A=(P,Σ,Ω,Π,τ,Ctx) combining the Step-7 epistemic state Σ (Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) with the new governance state Ω (SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus), keeping epistemic and governance dimensions separate.

rows.anchor: The acceptance lattice question ... Candidate, Supported, Accepted, Committed look like a ladder, but they are not universally ordered. Accepted\not\Rightarrow Committed. Contested can coexist with Accepted. AcceptanceStatus should be modeled as a state space, not a scalar hierarchy.
rows.statement: Corrects the apparent ladder Candidate→Supported→Accepted→Committed: it is not a universal ordering (Accepted⇏Committed; Contested can coexist with Accepted), so AcceptanceStatus must be a state space, not a scalar hierarchy.

rows.anchor: Mathematical structure ... \mathcal O=\mathcal O_S\times\mathcal O_A\times\mathcal O_C\times\mathcal O_X ... \Omega_A\in\mathcal O ... \omega: \Omega_A\times Event\times Policy \rightharpoonup \Omega_A
rows.statement: Formalizes the acceptance-status space as a product O=O_S×O_A×O_C×O_X (support/acceptance/commitment/contest statuses) with Ω_A∈O and a partial transition function ω:Ω_A×Event×Policy⇀Ω_A.

rows.anchor: The full KnowledgeOS epistemic pipeline ... Evidence → Evidence Relations → Evidence Assessment → Acceptance Policy → Accepted/Rejected/Unresolved → Authority/Purpose → Commitment → Knowledge State → Ideal State → Discrepancy → Next Acquisition. And the cycle repeats.
rows.statement: Assembles the full epistemic pipeline: Evidence→Relations→Assessment→AcceptancePolicy→{Accepted,Rejected,Unresolved}→Authority/Purpose→Commitment→KnowledgeState→IdealState→Discrepancy→NextAcquisition, cycling back.

rows.anchor: Step 8 verdict ... STRUCTURALLY RESOLVED ... a rigorous distinction between Evidence, Assessment, Support, Acceptance, Commitment, Truth. These should never be collapsed.
rows.statement: Declares Step 8 structurally resolved, having established a rigorous six-way distinction (Evidence/Assessment/Support/Acceptance/Commitment/Truth) that must never be collapsed.

rows.anchor: The flag is NON-DISCRIMINATING.
rows.statement: Observation O-5 assessed and CLEARED by test: the candidate's CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 flag is non-discriminating, proven by testing it against a known reference (the governance session itself carries the same flag with a distinct CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID); consequence: the flag cannot disqualify (not evidence of parentage/subagent status/prior participation) and cannot detect a subagent either -- detection remains by identity collision against the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (per a 2026-08-22 empirical probe), and candidate 84e5c1f7 collides with no barred identity.

rows.anchor: No transition was hand-composed.
rows.statement: Independence verified from primary evidence (git grep/log, filesystem search, no registered lane referencing the candidate in 23 workflow records) rather than candidate testimony alone; appointment executed canonically through next-actor-orchestration.php appoint (role-specific bars passed as --exclude arguments, so eligibility is recorded by mechanism, not by an author's judgement -- the property whose absence produced ASD-001); AST-018 wrote all three transitions (REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, seq 6-8) deriving predecessor/from from the fold's current owner rather than being hand-composed.

rows.anchor: I was wrong about START, and it changes what the human must do next
rows.statement: Correction C-1: the prior claim (stated in the REPAIR-001 authorization record, CONTEXT, the session log, and to the PO/ARB) that AST-018 appoint 'deliberately does not write START; G-3 stays human' was FALSE -- appointReviewer() writes three transitions (REGISTER, HANDOFF, and START at lines 430-447, recordedBy human, using the supplied --human-act) and then verifies ACTIVE from the fold; the prior reading stopped one block short of the START. Consequence: the implementation lane is already ACTIVE and authorized; the PO/ARB does not need to record a separate START.

lineage_claims.target: prior claim in REPAIR-001 authorization record §6, CONTEXT, session log, and implementer prompt
lineage_claims.quote: That was false.

rows.anchor: A second-order blemish I caused, recorded rather than tidied away.
rows.statement: Because the (mistaken) belief was that START would be a separate act, the --human-act text passed to the appointment carried a caveat denying it authorizes START; that same text is now recorded as the humanAct of seq 8, a START transition -- so the record contains a START whose own prose denies being a START authorization. The transition itself is held valid (the human act genuinely authorized the appointment, which AST-018 treats as the activation authority) but the prose is self-contradictory; per append-only discipline this is not rewritten, only corrected via this new record.

rows.anchor: AST-018 appoint collapses appointment and activation
rows.statement: Finding O-6: one human act produces REGISTER+HANDOFF+START with no appoint-without-activate path through AST-018 appoint, and the same --human-act string serves as both the appointment authority and the START authority; judged not a defect but documented business intent (the tool's purpose is to remove UUID/REGISTER/HANDOFF/START mechanics from the human), yet worth recording because a person authorizing an appointment thereby also authorizes the start, and the estate's own vocabulary/prompts had treated these as two separate gates -- 'the vocabulary and the mechanisms disagree.' Contrast: AST-019 activate also fuses REGISTER->HANDOFF->START. Status: RECORDED - NOT PROMOTED - NOT DECIDED (ES-006.1, first clean occurrence, methodology frozen), explicitly not a proposal to change AST-018 and not in REPAIR-001's scope.

rows.anchor: The FAIL verdict is ACCEPTED
rows.statement: PO/ARB accepts an independent verification's FAIL verdict on AST-019 as authoritative and final (not reopened, re-run, or rewritten); F-1 (a reachable correctness defect on the production write path) is confirmed independently at source: analyze() at lines 377-385 returns no fold key, so writeActivation() at lines 401-402 forces $owner to null, mis-deriving both REGISTER.predecessor and HANDOFF.from.

rows.anchor: CONTINUATION recorded (seq 5)
rows.statement: A CONTINUATION transition (requiring a registered session) reactivates the original verifier's lane solely as a handoff predecessor so the repair lane can receive its HANDOFF -- identical in shape to the parent item's seq-10 precedent where a STOPped verification lane was reactivated only to hand off to its successor; explicitly reopens the work item, not the verification/verdict/report, and the verifier performs no further work.

lineage_claims.quote: identical to the parent item's seq 10 precedent

rows.anchor: That advice is misleading in this state
rows.statement: Observation O-4 (reporting imprecision, not a defect claim): after the CONTINUATION, AST-018 next-actor reports 'LANE ACTIVE ... no new actor is needed', which is misleading in this state since the lane is ACTIVE only as a mechanical consequence of the continuation, not because the verifier has further work; the fold itself is correct, only the advisory interpretation is wrong; verified harmless to the plan since appointReviewer() has no active-lane refusal (unlike AST-019's GO-13 gate). Status: RECORDED, NOT PROMOTED (ES-006.1, single occurrence).

rows.anchor: REPAIR-001 AUTHORIZED (grant G-REPAIR-001)
rows.statement: Grant G-REPAIR-001 authorizes a narrowly scoped repair covering four findings and one test gap on a single file plus its contract test: F-1 (blocking: analyze() omits fold, forcing null mutationOwner and mis-deriving predecessor/from), F-3 (failure path returns the refusal() shape lacking the ok key the caller tests), F-4 (transitionWritten hard-coded true when nothing was written), F-2 (PHP warnings on STDOUT break the --json contract, closing only when BOTH F-1 and F-3 are fixed -- not a corollary of F-1 alone), and O-1 (a RED-first contract test with a live non-null mutationOwner asserting REGISTER.predecessor and HANDOFF.from both equal owner, failing on today's code before any fix). Touchable scope: activate-commissioned-fresh-session.php and its contract test only.

rows.anchor: F-5 is HELD OUTSIDE this repair
rows.statement: F-5 (whether KOS_MECHANISM_PATH may redirect the 'sole writer', and why AST-017/AST-018 use hard constants while AST-019 does not) is explicitly held outside REPAIR-001 pending a separate Architecture decision -- must not be fixed, mitigated, or documented away inside the repair, since a correctness slice silently settling an architecture question is a category slippage the estate forbids; ASD-001 is preserved as a recorded sequencing defect (not reopened/remedied/erased), found to be the same defect class as F-1 from opposite directions (O-3); verification history (seq 1-4) stays untouched; the adopted parent layers L1+L2+L3's byte-integrity is stated as an acceptance criterion of REPAIR-001, not an assumption.

rows.anchor: Independence requirements differ by role -- kept separate deliberately
rows.statement: Independence bars differ by role and are kept separate deliberately: the REPAIR-001 implementer is barred only from being the verifier (must not repair what it verified, R-34/EP-02) or the governance process that scoped the slice, while the original AST-019 producer is explicitly NOT categorically barred from implementing (repairing one's own code is ordinary engineering); re-verification afterwards bars the first verifier, the producer, the scoping governance process, AND whoever implements REPAIR-001, since independence from the work under check is what makes the check worth anything -- collapsing verification-role bars onto implementation-role bars would shrink the eligible pool for no governed reason.

rows.anchor: declaration-only prompt. This is NOT the repair commission.
rows.statement: A two-phase actor-onboarding pattern is used: Phase 1 is a declaration-only prompt in which a candidate determines its own process identity from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and discloses independence before reading any subject material; Phase 2 (the actual repair commission) issues only after appointment, human START, and an approved EP-01 plan -- explicitly designed so a declaration arriving with a plan attached is judged to have already broken the boundary the prompt exists to protect.

rows.anchor: the actual test is PARTICIPATION, not identity
rows.statement: A different runtime session UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence, since a restarted process can report a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining the same working context (observation O-5); the actual eligibility test is participation ('have I authored, scoped, reviewed, verified, analysed, or advised on this work item or subject in this conversation or any context I carry'), to be disclosed in full even if it makes the candidate ineligible, with the identifier list treated only as a non-exhaustive aid.

rows.anchor: Two statements, both true
rows.statement: The original AST-019 producer is kept distinct on two levels: the general rule is that it is NOT categorically barred from implementing its own repair (ordinary engineering, no rule bars it), while the PO/ARB has separately excluded it for this specific slice as 'not the cleanest separation for this defect'; a candidate matching that identity must report NOT ELIGIBLE citing the PO/ARB decision, not a rule, and is also barred from the later re-verification.

rows.anchor: 84c0f6f6 was handed the full commission at first start and, following it in order, read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
rows.statement: The declaration-only prompt design (step 0 'declare before you orient' placed first) is a direct correction of an earlier failure mode: a prior candidate (84c0f6f6), handed the full commission at first start, read approximately 120 lines of the subject before declaring, traced to prompt selection (structuring) rather than process error; the AMENDMENT-001 changelog also records bars becoming participation-first (UUIDs demoted to a non-exhaustive aid), a new barred id (e40f3fd0) added after the scoping process itself restarted under a new runtime id, and the return format extended with REQUESTED ROLE/REPAIR GRANT/NON-ACTIONS/explicit STOP fields.

rows.anchor: the implementation STOP is unrecorded
rows.statement: Governance determination that the actual next governed act precedes any re-verifier: the repair (commit d8a5ee93, +22/-5 plus a 293-line contract test) exists in git but the authoritative workflow record never recorded the implementation lane's STOP (lane 84e5c1f7 still ACTIVE); consequence if skipped: appoint would still mechanically work but the implementer's IMPLEMENTED report and evidence would never enter the record, existing only as a git commit -- exactly the fact/record separation the estate protects. Canonical chain: implementation STOP (reports IMPLEMENTED, never VERIFIED) -> item becomes STOPPED -> human CONTINUATION -> AST-018 appoint the re-verifier.

rows.anchor: Is independent re-verification binding? YES
rows.statement: Determination that independent re-verification of the repaired code is binding, grounded primarily in a quoted PO/ARB authorization clause ('keep AST-019/AMENDMENT-001 not adopted and not authorized pending independent verification') that has never been lifted; reasoning that a verification of superseded (pre-repair) code cannot be the verification of the code that replaced it, so a prior FAIL verdict does not discharge the condition -- the repair is what makes the condition answerable. Substantive reason: defect F-1 was invisible to the entire prior 25-test contract suite, and the new tests certifying the fix (GO-26..GO-30) were written by the same process that wrote the fix, so the only present evidence of a cure comes from the party being certified -- explicitly NOT generalized into a rule that every implementation requires fresh verification, resting on this one named condition attached to this one named asset plus a blocking FAIL whose defect the existing suite could not see.

rows.anchor: fresh runtime UUID ≠ absence of prior participation
rows.statement: Restates and applies the accumulated independence-detection findings (a subagent reports its parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so collision with a barred identity disqualifies; CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 is non-discriminating per O-5, disclosed but neither disqualifying nor certifying; prior participation established from primary evidence searches, not UUID novelty) to bar four named identities (the REPAIR-001 implementer, the first verifier, the AST-019 producer, and the scoping governance process) from re-verification, each for a stated reason rather than by reflex.

rows.anchor: A previous candidate was handed the full commission at first start ... and read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
rows.statement: A second declaration-only Phase-1 prompt (for the re-verifier role) reapplies the 'declare before you orient' pattern established for the implementer (S0413), explicitly citing the same prior ordering-deviation incident as its rationale; requires the candidate to search for its own id via git grep/log and directory scans before reading any authoritative state, and to report identity/independence/prior-participation/eligibility/work-item-state/authorization in a fixed six-field format before stopping.

rows.anchor: recordedBy: governance, deliberately not implementation
rows.statement: Governance closes the implementation lane's STOP itself, but by TRANSCRIBING the lane's own already-existing completion report (commit d8a5ee93, its message, the EP-01 plan, developer guide, session log) rather than speaking in the lane's voice, per INV-ATTR-1/2; explicitly asserts only that the completion report exists and is cited, not that the repair is correct (auditing correctness would be Governance performing the verification it is commissioning); status recorded as IMPLEMENTED -- explicitly NOT VERIFIED, NOT ADOPTED, NOT AUTHORIZED.

rows.anchor: An identity cannot be invented
rows.statement: The work item is narrowly reopened (CONTINUATION, seq 10) to admit a re-verification lane, reactivating the mutation owner solely as a HANDOFF predecessor (mirroring the seq-5 precedent), without reopening the implementation scope, the prior FAIL verdict, or the parent item; no appointment is made because 'an identity cannot be invented' (INV-ATTR-1/2) and AST-018 refuses to appoint without a candidate -- 'a fresh actor has no identity until its own process reports one', so the next act is necessarily a human starting a fresh session with the declaration-only prompt.

rows.anchor: The candidate's declaration was not available to Governance.
rows.statement: Re-verifier be8aecec is appointed even though its declaration text was never supplied to Governance (no document found on disk); Governance explicitly discloses it did not assess the candidate's self-disclosed compliance facts (step-0 ordering, child-session disclosure, participation searches, bootstrap results) and states acceptance rests only on binding identity criteria verifiable from primary evidence (identity collision against four bars, zero footprint across four searches, exclusions passed to the engine) plus the PO/ARB's direction -- the gap is disclosed, not papered over, and an obligation is placed on the appointed lane to record its declaration verbatim as its first act.

rows.anchor: PASS WITH FINDINGS
rows.statement: Independent re-verification of REPAIR-001 reaches PASS WITH FINDINGS after the verifier independently reproduces the pre-repair failure from committed pre-repair source (b9369797) in a disposable worktree -- check=READY then activate=exit 65 INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE, written=[REGISTER], REGISTER.predecessor=null, HANDOFF refused, orphan stranded CREATED, unparseable --json -- and then confirms post-repair success on the authoritative record itself (REGISTER.predecessor='OWNER', HANDOFF.from='OWNER', lane ACTIVE, exactly 3 transitions, no orphan, valid JSON with zero diagnostics), rather than trusting the ACTIVATED result string; GO-26..GO-30 independently confirmed 5/5 RED against pre-repair code and green at HEAD with a +293/-0 test diff so GO-01..GO-25 were not weakened.

experiment.hypothesis: REPAIR-001's fix genuinely closes the F-1 defect (null mutationOwner on the write path) without regressing existing behavior.
experiment.setup: A disposable detached git worktree at the pre-repair commit (b9369797) and the current HEAD (d8a5ee93), both exercised with an identical hermetic fixture presenting a live mutationOwner.
experiment.assumptions: The implementer's RED-first claim should not be taken on trust.
experiment.inputs: An armed fixture built through AST-015 append calls only (never hand-written JSON); a forwarding proxy (rv-race.php) to force a concurrent-ownership race.
experiment.method: Run check/activate on both commits, inspect the authoritative workflow record (not just exit codes/result strings), re-run the full GO-01..GO-30 contract suite and the full WorkflowEngine regression suite, and force a race condition with rv-race.php.
experiment.result: Pre-repair: exit 65, orphan REGISTER, unparseable JSON. Post-repair: exit 0, correct ownership provenance, valid JSON. Regression 147/1577->152/1709 with no new failures. A forced race still produces a fail-closed, honestly-reported orphan (RV-F1), non-blocking.
experiment.interpretation: The repair genuinely fixes the reported defect and improves (does not merely mask) the failure-closed behavior under concurrency, though a non-atomic three-append sequence remains an architectural property outside this repair's scope.
experiment.limitations: RV-F1 (orphan under genuine concurrent ownership mutation) and RV-F2 (committed tests don't cover the live-owner partial-write combination) remain as non-blocking residual risks.
experiment.conclusion: PASS WITH FINDINGS: the defect is fixed and boundaries preserved; three non-blocking findings (RV-F1, RV-F2, RV-O3) are recorded but do not defeat the repair objective.

rows.anchor: RV-F1 · Orphan REGISTER when ownership moves between analysis and write
rows.statement: Finding RV-F1: because ownership is derived during analysis while the write is three separate non-atomic AST-015 appends, a genuine concurrent ownership change between analysis and write still produces an orphan REGISTER with a stale predecessor and a refused HANDOFF; forced deliberately with a custom rv-race.php tool; judged non-blocking because it is a strict improvement over pre-repair behavior (where the identical orphan occurred deterministically on every live-owner activation) and the failure is now fail-closed and honestly reported rather than silently wrong; the non-atomicity is classified as a pre-existing architectural property outside F-1..F-4/O-1, recommended as a separate future Architecture item.

rows.anchor: RV-F2 · Committed failure-path tests do not cover the live-owner combination
rows.statement: Finding RV-F2: the committed GO-27/GO-28/GO-30 tests use a null-owner fixture, so the precise 'partial write with a live owner' combination that F-1 inhabited is not covered by the committed suite even though independently exercised (and passing) in this verification report; judged non-blocking (no defect, but future-regression risk since the assurance rests on the report rather than a committed test), with a recommendation to extend the fixtures to armedOwnerFixture() in a future authorized slice. Finding RV-O3 confirms F-5 (mechanismPath() honoring KOS_MECHANISM_PATH) remains genuinely untouched by the repair diff, evidence of scope discipline rather than a defect.

rows.anchor: STOPPED does not obstruct the decision.
rows.statement: Governance recommends adoption is eligible (the §38 condition precedent 'pending independent verification' is now satisfied by a PASS verdict) while explicitly refusing to itself adopt, per R-34/EP-02; establishes that a STOPPED workItemState does not obstruct an adoption decision (precedent: the parent item was also STOPPED when adopted, recorded as governance decision documents, not workflow transitions); evaluates each of RV-F1/RV-F2/RV-O3 against a search for a binding rule that would make a non-blocking finding block adoption and finds none -- the estate's own practice (AST-015 qualified-with-conditions; the parent adopted with F-2/F-4/F-5 open) is 'adoption carrying recorded findings is the established pattern, findings are carried, not resolved as a precondition.'

rows.anchor: Adoption answers "is this our accepted asset?" ... Authorization for future use answers "may it now be used?"
rows.statement: Distinguishes Adoption ('is this our accepted asset?' -- a judgement about the artifact and its evidence) from Authorization for future use ('may it now be used?' -- a judgement about operating risk), citing the parent item's own precedent that adoption and authorization are separate explicit human acts which Governance can never collapse or infer from each other (§38); RV-F1 is classified as bearing on the second question (a use-time risk that can only materialize once the asset is actually invoked under concurrent ownership mutation), so it belongs in the authorization decision rather than blocking adoption.

lineage_claims.quote: From the parent's own adoption record ... 'The human said adopt; they said nothing about authorization for future use.'

rows.anchor: Authorization is unconditioned.
rows.statement: PO/ARB authorizes AST-019 for future use plainly and unconditionally (declining an offered qualification-with-conditions shape); authorization permits AST-019's use (fresh session self-binding to an already-commissioned responsibility via activate, with check as read-only preflight) without creating any wiring, hook, or automatic invocation (runtime_moments stays ON_DEMAND, mirroring AST-016's adoption discipline), and without making AST-019 the only activation route (AST-018 appoint remains the canonical appointment mechanism). RV-F1 is explicitly stated as the risk this authorization knowingly accepts, now live because authorization is the act that permits use; it is recorded as UNOWNED (no follow-up work commissioned), alongside RV-F2, both explicitly requiring a future human act to become tracked work.

rows.statement: PO/ARB formally adopts AST-019/ActivateCommissionedFreshSession (domain concept BindRuntimeToRequestedResponsibility) as repaired at commit d8a5ee93, discharging the §38 condition precedent via the PASS WITH FINDINGS re-verification; the decision explicitly rests not on green tests but on the independently-established pre-repair-failure/post-repair-success comparison and on preserved separation of duties across five distinct identities (producer/implementer/first-verifier/re-verifier/scoping-governance), each bar enforced through AST-018's --exclude mechanism rather than an author's judgement; three non-blocking findings (RV-F1/RV-F2/RV-O3) are carried into adoption, not resolved, consistent with the estate's established practice; this adoption record explicitly does not authorize use (a separate act), does not resolve any open finding, and does not reopen the first verification's FAIL verdict or the parent item.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Is independent re-verification binding? YES
rationale_evidence.statement: Determination that independent re-verification of the repaired code is binding, grounded primarily in a quoted PO/ARB authorization clause ('keep AST-019/AMENDMENT-001 not adopted and not authorized pending independent verification') that has never been lifted; reasoning that a verification of superseded (pre-repair) code cannot be the verification of the code that replaced it, so a prior FAIL verdict does not discharge the condition -- the repair is what makes the condition answerable. Substantive reason: defect F-1 was invisible to the entire prior 25-test contract suite, and the new tests certifying the fix (GO-26..GO-30) were written by the same process that wrote the fix, so the only present evidence of a cure comes from the party being certified -- explicitly NOT generalized into a rule that every implementation requires fresh verification, resting on this one named condition attached to this one named asset plus a blocking FAIL whose defect the existing suite could not see.

sources.note: Step 143/144's six-phase evolution sequence, seven-item anti-pattern list, Before/After redefinition of engineering knowledge, and the planned first-vertical-slice reference implementation (Governed Decision->Rule->Agent Context->Action->Evidence->Verification->Finding).

rows.statement: Defines a six-phase evolution sequence (not implementing all twenty work packages simultaneously), with each phase's rationale: Phase 1 establishes Identity/Ownership/Authority/Validity (without which the graph merely connects ambiguous objects); Phase 2 formalizes Decision/Policy/Exception/Claim with documents becoming projections; Phase 3 formalizes Evidence/Observation/Rule/Verification/Finding, connecting existing checks; Phase 4 introduces the Assurance Graph and Context Service once underlying semantics are stable (ordering important); Phase 5 connects Agent->Action->Authorization->Execution for governed agentic engineering; Phase 6 makes KnowledgeOS a subject of its own assurance model for continuous architecture governance.

rows.anchor: CURRENT{Agents,Governance,Checks} → FORMALIZATION{Authority,Evidence,Rules} → RELATIONSHIP → ASSURANCE GRAPH → GOVERNED CONTEXT → GOVERNED AGENT → AUTHORIZED ACTION → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → GOVERNANCE.
rows.statement: Summarizes the entire evolution as a single transformation-architecture diagram from current mechanisms through formalization, relationship-building, the graph, governed context/agent, authorized action, evidence, verification, and back to governance.

rows.anchor: Do not: RewriteEverything, MakeEverythingAMicroservice, MakeTheGraphTheDatabaseOfEverything, PutAllKnowledgeIntoAgentMemory, LetLLMJudgmentReplaceDeterministicChecks, AllowAgentsToBypassAuthorization, CopyExternalSystemModelsIntoTheDomain.
rows.statement: Lists seven tempting-but-incorrect implementation anti-patterns for the target system, derived from the entire delta analysis.

rows.anchor: Before: EngineeringKnowledge = Files+Scripts+Memory+Logs+HumanUnderstanding. After: EngineeringKnowledge = GovernedSemanticObjects+Evidence+Relationships+ExplicitAuthority.
rows.statement: States the deepest transformation as a Before/After redefinition of engineering knowledge itself, with files/scripts/agents remaining important interfaces and projections rather than the substance.

rows.anchor: Documents → Machine-addressable semantic knowledge. AI Agent → Governed Engineering Actor. Compliance → Continuous Engineering Assurance.
rows.statement: Explicitly rejects three reductive framings of the transformation — 'documents -> better documents' (it's documents -> machine-addressable semantic knowledge), 'chatbot -> better chatbot' (it's AI Agent -> Governed Engineering Actor), 'compliance engine' (it's compliance -> continuous engineering assurance spanning architecture/development/CI/deployment/runtime/evidence/governance) — and states the most concise description: KnowledgeOS evolves from a collection of AI-engineering knowledge/governance mechanisms into a governed semantic engineering platform.

rows.anchor: Authority, Identity, Provenance, Relationships, Verification, Authorization — the most important changes are semantic, not technological.
rows.statement: Step 143 verdict: the six most important semantic changes, after which existing Claude/Codex tooling, registry, deterministic checks, hooks, session logging, and engineering integrations can be progressively connected rather than replaced.

rows.anchor: 1. Architecture workstreams ... 10. The first vertical slice. Governed Decision → Rule → Agent Context → Action → Evidence → Verification → Finding.
rows.statement: Opens Step 144 (KnowledgeOS Evolution Roadmap): a ten-item roadmap-definition list (workstreams, dependencies, MVP boundary, what can start immediately, what awaits semantic decisions, artifact migration, untouched mechanisms, phase acceptance criteria, architecture fitness tests, first vertical slice); identifies the most important next decision as the first vertical slice — proving the architecture end-to-end with one real scenario (Governed Decision -> Rule -> Agent Context -> Action -> Evidence -> Verification -> Finding) as the reference implementation.

rows.anchor: Do not build KnowledgeOS horizontally. Build one complete governed engineering loop.
rows.statement: States the central roadmap rule and the full first-vertical-slice chain (Governed Decision->Applicable Rule->Governed Agent Context->Agent Recommendation->Action Request->Authorization->Execution->Evidence->Verification->Finding->Governance), 'the smallest slice that demonstrates the actual architectural thesis.'

rows.anchor: Nexus as reference domain, not merely an example.
rows.statement: Chooses Nexus as the vertical-slice subject because existing KnowledgeOS work already covers infrastructure discovery, version info, repository/blob-store info, runtime info, network info, migration requirements, governance questions, and architecture/change-management concerns — spanning Business/Architecture/Infrastructure/Security/Operations/Governance knowledge; but requires starting with Read->Analyze->Verify, not Agent->Production->Modify Nexus, to prove the semantic/assurance architecture without unnecessary operational risk.

rows.anchor: Vertical Slice 0: Can KnowledgeOS determine the current governed state of Nexus and explain the evidence supporting that state?
rows.statement: Vertical Slice 0 (read-only context query) with output schema (applicable governance, applicable knowledge, current observations, supporting evidence, applicable rules, verification results, open findings) and acceptance criterion that every context item carries Identity/Source/Authority/Validity/Provenance.

rows.anchor: Vertical Slice 1: Evaluate a specific Nexus fitness rule (NexusVersionMustBeSupported). Rule → Nexus Adapter → Observation → Evidence → Verification → PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.

rows.statement: Vertical Slice 2 introduces the agent, with a worked recommendation example ('the planned Nexus upgrade should proceed only after infrastructure prerequisites X and Y have been verified') and the acceptance traversal explaining why the recommendation was made.

rows.anchor: Vertical Slice 3: RequestAction evaluated by Authorization; agent does not directly execute. REQUESTED/AUTHORIZED/EXECUTED as three distinct states.

rows.statement: WS3 (Evidence & Assurance) acceptance criterion connecting existing deterministic checks to formal Evidence/Observation/FitnessRule/Verification/Finding concepts.

rows.anchor: Read-only → Non-destructive mutation → Staging → Production with approval.
rows.statement: WS6 (Authorization & Execution): a four-step incremental risk ladder for introducing the Request->Authorize->Execute governed action boundary, starting with low-risk read-only actions.

rows.anchor: Architecture boundary check, Event/outbox consistency, Graph projection freshness, Evidence integrity, Agent contract compliance, Authorization bypass detection.
rows.statement: WS7 (Self-Assurance): once the first loop works, KnowledgeOS becomes subject to its own assurance rules via six example self-checks.

rows.anchor: WS1 → {WS2, WS3} → WS4 → WS5 → WS6 → WS7. Do not scale agent access before authority is defined. Governance → Assurance. Verdict → Evidence.
rows.statement: Presents the workstream dependency graph and justifies the ordering: Agent Integration is not first because 'if the semantic foundation is unstable, the agents simply automate ambiguity' (do not scale agent access before authority is defined); the Graph is not first because a graph of poorly defined semantics produces 'fast confusion,' needing stable identities/ownership/relationships first; Governance is early because it defines ExpectedState (without which assurance has nothing authoritative to compare against, Governance->Assurance); Evidence is early because without it Verification becomes a bare assertion (Verdict->Evidence required).

rows.anchor: MVP = one governed engineering scenario with complete traceability, not a full enterprise platform.
rows.statement: Redefines the KnowledgeOS MVP and gives a ten-question success criterion (what was expected/why/what did the agent know/recommend/who authorized/what happened/what evidence proves it/was it compliant/what finding/what governance decision followed) — 'if all ten can be answered, the architecture has been proven.'

rows.anchor: Wave 1 high-value governance artifacts ... Wave 5 external-system observations. Structured Knowledge Object with sourceArtifact → Original Document (never delete).
rows.statement: Defines a five-wave migration strategy avoiding a 'big bang' migration, with the rule that migration never means deleting old documents — a structured knowledge object retains a sourceArtifact reference preserving historical context.

rows.anchor: Useful local context, Candidate knowledge, Verified knowledge, Obsolete, Unknown. Memory → CandidateClaim → Evidence → Verification → GovernedKnowledge. AgentOutput ⇏ Knowledge.
rows.statement: Defines a five-way memory-item migration classification and the target promotion workflow, with the anti-automatic-promotion principle: the platform must never assume LLMGeneratedText=Truth — evidence and verification, not agent output alone, determine promotion.

sources.note: A proposed (not yet HPA-adopted) protocol defining the one lawful path by which a theory/independent-verification result may become book content, grounded in 'Research discovers · Verification tests · Governance decides · The book records.' Ten entry conditions must all hold before any book change is drafted (stable filesystem artifact identity with md5+counts; explicit per-claim evidence classes; findings separated from interpretations; unresolved items listed; contradictions preserved not harmonized; class-4/5 changes routed out of the book lane; no claim promoted merely by appearing in the report). A six-step procedure (Receive→Classify→Route→Await ruling→Draft→Verify) and permanent prohibitions follow (the book never rules on a theory question, never treats an AI-produced report as evidence, never edits a frozen/historical artifact to agree with a later finding), plus a production-freeze rule for reports arriving mid-Part-production.

rows.anchor:
Rows expanded after repository inspection. **Every row is "Automatic? No" and "Requires human
 authorization? Yes" — this is the invariant of the matrix, not a coincidence of its rows.**
rows.statement: The book<->theory change-impact matrix's structural invariant, stated explicitly: across all 12 possible future-theory-outcome rows (theory remains open; an OQ resolves; a candidate is refuted; a result becomes TESTED; the mathematical model changes; architecture correspondence changes; a historical contradiction is exposed; closure is found unjustified; a book claim is contradicted; a new OQ is produced; implementation correspondence is asserted for a formal object; a report is AI-produced with no independent artifact), every single row requires human authorization and none is automatic — this is a designed invariant of the matrix, not an incidental pattern.

rows.anchor: | 12 | Report is itself AI-produced with no independent artifact | **no book impact whatsoever**
rows.statement: Row 12 states the matrix's strongest prohibition in concrete form: a verification report that is itself AI-produced with no independent artifact has NO book impact whatsoever — it is recorded as received but not consumed, per the echo rule and BA-ED2-14.

rows.anchor:
**Standing rule it enforces:** *Research discovers · Verification tests · Governance decides ·
 The book records.*
rows.statement: Standing governance principle: Research discovers, Verification tests, Governance decides, The book records — the book lane never performs the first three functions, and a report's mere existence is never evidence for its content.

rows.anchor: | 9 | **No claim promoted merely by appearing in the report.**
rows.statement: Entry condition 9: no claim may be promoted (e.g. NOT ESTABLISHED -> TESTED, or an OQ closing) merely by appearing in a verification report — an explicit HPA/architecture-lane ruling is required first, and the book may only ever report 'that a lane asserts X', never 'that X holds', until such a ruling exists.

rows.anchor: ## Freeze rule (mid-production arrival)
rows.statement: Freeze rule: if a verification report arrives while a book Part is in production, the affected chapters are frozen at their current artifact identity until the ruling step (S4) completes, and production may continue only on chapters the synchronization findings do not touch — introduced because IV.4, the open-questions chapter, is precisely the one a verification result would move.

rows.anchor: > **Part II records the research history and is accepted. The theory is under controlled verification. The next book work should be synthesis and operationalization, not premature theory closure.**
rows.statement: Directive establishing a book-production phase transition: Part II (research history) stays frozen/accepted and must not be rewritten merely because later theory work (Step 281/282/verification) produced newer findings, unless the synchronization gate explicitly rules that a later finding changes the historical account; the next phase of book work should be synthesis and operationalization rather than declaring the theory closed.
invariants: book acceptance is distinct from theory correctness

rows.anchor:
## 4. Explicit status separation

Maintain these four independent dimensions:

1. Formal closure
2. Computational closure
3. Empirical closure
4. Governance closure

Never collapse them into one "verified" or "closed" status.
rows.statement: The book session is directed to maintain four independent status dimensions (formal, computational, empirical, governance closure) and never collapse them into a single 'verified'/'closed' status, with the explicit chained inequalities FORMALLY CLOSED != IMPLEMENTED, IMPLEMENTED != EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED, EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED != GOVERNANCE-RATIFIED, BOOK ACCEPTED != THEORY CORRECT.

rows.anchor:
## 3. First deliverable — canonical theory-to-book registry

Before writing substantial new Part III/IV prose, create:

`THEORY-TO-BOOK-CANONICAL-STATE.md`

This is the controlled bridge between theory verification and book production.
rows.statement: Commissions THEORY-TO-BOOK-CANONICAL-STATE.md as the first required deliverable before any substantial new Part III/IV prose, specifying its required fields per construct (canonical name, canonical definition, source artifact(s), current/formal/computational/empirical/governance status, evidence class, relevant OQ, relevant verification result, whether it may appear in book prose, permitted wording strength, blocked wording, intended chapter), and directing that missing values must not be inferred but recorded using explicit placeholder statuses (NOT ESTABLISHED, OPEN, BLOCKED, GOVERNANCE DECISION REQUIRED).

lineage_claims.quote: Begin with `THEORY-TO-BOOK-CANONICAL-STATE.md`, then proceed through the existing synchronization gate.

rows.statement: Eight explicit prohibitions on the book-production session: no unrestricted gap-discovery pass, no inventing new theoretical constructs, no declaring the theory complete, no promoting an Open Question without an authorized ruling, no upgrading an evidence class merely because a verification artifact exists, no treating a verification session's conclusion as automatically book-authoritative, no modifying ratified architecture/governance decisions, and no resolving governance questions itself; if a theory or governance issue is encountered it must be recorded as a dependency and the session must stop at the synchronization boundary.

Eight explicit stop conditions requiring the book session to halt and request synchronization/ruling rather than proceed unilaterally: a new theoretical claim being required; an OQ needing a status change; an evidence class needing upgrade; a governance contradiction needing resolution; O_core needing authoritative freezing; a formal construct needing to be changed (not merely documented); accepted Part II wording needing historical alteration; or the four-way closure distinction becoming ambiguous.

Symbol counts over root B's **governed** artifacts (v0.2 AUTHORIZED; FA-1/FA-3/FA-6 RATIFIED):

rows.statement: A mechanical symbol-occurrence check across root-B's governed, ratified artifacts (v0.2 authorized; FA-1/FA-3/FA-6 ratified) finds ZERO occurrences of the verification lane's symbols A (script-A assertion set), R (relations), Sigma, Q_t, O (operation universe), Provenance, Replay, or Measurement; the ratified model's K_t is a state over 8 different primitives {Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action}, graded TESTED (within scope), and is a DIFFERENT OBJECT from the verification lane's K=(A,R); the only construct in this registry carrying an explicit governance act is Policy (GN-19/R-1/I-11). Consequence for the book: the produced Part III teaches the ratified architecture, and the verification lane's constructs cannot be substituted into it.

experiment.hypothesis: The book's ratified theory vocabulary (v0.2, FA-1/FA-3/FA-6) and the independent verification lane's vocabulary refer to the same underlying constructs under different names.
experiment.setup: Search root-B's governed, ratified artifacts for occurrences of eight verification-lane symbols.
experiment.assumptions: A symbol's occurrence count of 0 in the ratified artifacts is evidence of a genuinely different (not merely renamed) object.
experiment.inputs: The set of governed v0.1/v0.2/FA-1/FA-3/FA-6 artifacts.
experiment.method: Mechanical text search for each symbol.
experiment.result: 0 occurrences for every one of the eight symbols across every ratified artifact checked.
experiment.interpretation: The two lanes' vocabularies do not overlap at all at the symbol level; the ratified K_t and the verification lane's K are different objects, not two names for one thing.
experiment.limitations: A symbol search does not rule out the two objects being conceptually equivalent under a translation; the finding is about vocabulary/artifact non-overlap, argued to have book-writing consequences regardless.
experiment.conclusion: The verification lane's constructs must not be substituted into book prose that teaches the ratified v0.2/K_t architecture.

What KnowledgeOS research discovered and how the model evolved.

What the governed KnowledgeOS architecture actually defines.

What an engineer must build and what evidence demonstrates that it exists.

sources.note: A formal 22-definition consolidation building directly on the same-day Goswami-Rao measure-theory extraction: defines Knowledge Space as a measurable space KS=(X,A) built from an index set J of admissible epistemic observables Y_j (never a probability space by default), with a representation map Gamma:K -> A giving a compatibility region for each Knowledge State, an information filtration F_t, a probabilistic assessment Pi_t=L(Z|F_t) kept distinct from K_t, an Ideal State I_t=I(Q_t,C_t,S_t,EC_t), a typed (not scalar-subtraction) Knowledge Gap Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t;Q_t,C_t,EC_t), Zero as an indicator predicate 1[K_t models EC_t], a (possibly probabilistic) transition T_t, a trajectory space Omega_K=prod X_t with process probability space (Omega_K,A_K,P_K), observer-specific filtrations F_t^S, a semantic-equivalence relation r1=_sem r2 via matching observable behaviour B_r, and an explicit four-way non-collapse syntactic-equality != representation-equality != semantic-equivalence != almost-sure-equality. Concludes the 13-vs-8 kernel-reduction instability arose from attempting kernel minimality before X, A, =_sem, K, D and T were fixed, and reframes the next research question from 'what is Knowledge Space' to 'what is the minimal admissible family of epistemic observables {Y_j} that generates (X,A)'. Possibly the same architecture as this batch's goswami-rao-measure-theoretic-knowledge-space-architecture (produced the same day, explicitly building on it), possibly a distinct, more formalized successor artifact -- not resolved within this batch.

rows.anchor: Do not define Knowledge Space merely as an infinite set of knowledge elements, and do not define it directly as a probability space. Define it first as a measurable space of possible epistemic configurations. Probability, filtration, conditional assessment, and trajectories are additional structures built on top of it.
rows.statement: States the file's central recommendation superseding earlier candidate definitions: Knowledge Space must be defined first as a measurable space of possible epistemic configurations, never directly as a probability space nor as a bare set of knowledge elements; probability, filtration, conditional assessment and trajectories are all additional structures layered on top.

rows.anchor: Let \(J\) be an index set of admissible epistemic observables. For every j in J, define a measurable value space (V_j,B_j). An epistemic observable is a map $$Y_j:\Omega\rightarrow\mathcal V_j$$ ... observable != knowledge and observable != dimension automatically.
rows.statement: Defines Epistemic Observable: for an index set J of admissible epistemic observables, each j in J has a measurable value space (V_j,B_j) and an observable map Y_j:Omega->V_j extracting an epistemically meaningful aspect of a state (worked examples: OS, RAM, Port); explicitly non-identical to knowledge or to dimension, preserving a Sentence->Proposition->Observable->Value chain.

rows.anchor: define the **epistemic configuration space** $$\mathcal X=\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal V_j$$ with product σ-field $$\mathscr A=\bigotimes_{j\in J}\mathscr B_j.$$ Thus (X,A) is the **measurable Knowledge Space**. ... not (X,A,P). Probability comes later.
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge-State Space as the product X = product over j in J of V_j with the product sigma-field A = tensor product of B_j, giving the measurable Knowledge Space (X,A) explicitly WITHOUT a probability measure attached -- probability is deferred to a later, separate definition.

rows.anchor: $$A_{\mathrm{RHEL9.8}}=\pi_{\mathrm{OS}}^{-1}(\{\mathrm{RHEL9.8}\}).$$ Proposition != Epistemic Event != Probability. A proposition has semantic content. An event is a measurable mathematical subset. A probability is a numerical measure assigned to that event.
rows.statement: Defines an Epistemic Event as a measurable subset A in the sigma-field A (worked as a coordinate-projection preimage), giving a precise three-way non-collapse Proposition != Epistemic Event != Probability: a proposition has semantic content, an event is a measurable mathematical subset, and a probability is a numerical measure assigned to that event.

rows.anchor: $$C_t=\{x\in\mathcal X: \pi_1(x)=a_1,\pi_2(x)=a_2,\pi_3(x)=a_3\}$$ ... a **finite-dimensional cylinder**. ... Unknown coordinate = coordinate not constrained by current epistemic information. Therefore: Unknown != False and Unknown != Zero probability.
rows.statement: Defines Partial Knowledge via a finite-dimensional cylinder set C_t (constraining finitely many coordinates while leaving the rest of X unrestricted), giving a rigorous definition of 'unknown coordinate' as one not constrained by current epistemic information -- reinforcing Unknown != False and Unknown != Zero-probability with a concrete measure-theoretic construction, stronger than merely storing an 'unknown' database value.

rows.anchor: define a representation map $$\Gamma:\mathcal K\rightarrow\mathscr A$$ ... $$\Gamma(K_t)\in\mathscr A$$ as the set of epistemic configurations compatible with K_t. ... possible configuration != current epistemic knowledge about that configuration.
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge State via a representation map Gamma: K -> A mapping each admissible Knowledge State K_t (from the separate space K of admissible Knowledge States) to its compatibility region Gamma(K_t) in A (the set of epistemic configurations consistent with it) -- a major improvement over simply writing K_t in X, since it distinguishes a possible configuration from current epistemic knowledge ABOUT that configuration.

rows.anchor: $$\mathcal F_t=\sigma(\text{all epistemically available observables through }t).$$ Then F_0 subset F_1 subset ... is a filtration. ... Evidence is a collection. F_t is the **closure of measurable information generated by that collection**.
rows.statement: Defines Epistemic Information as a sigma-field filtration F_t=sigma(all epistemically available observables through t) with F_0 subset F_1 subset ..., explicitly distinguished from a bare evidence collection E_t={e_1,...,e_n}: F_t is the closure of measurable information generated by that collection, a strictly stronger object.

rows.anchor: $$\Pi_t=\mathcal L(Z\mid\mathcal F_t).$$ Here Pi_t is a conditional distribution. ... but: Pi_t != K_t. This is crucial. Probability describes uncertainty. Knowledge describes the semantically determined epistemic state.
rows.statement: Defines Epistemic Assessment Pi_t=L(Z|F_t) as the conditional distribution of a latent measurable state variable Z given available information F_t, on an underlying probability space (Omega,G,P) -- explicitly Pi_t != K_t: probability describes uncertainty while Knowledge describes the semantically determined epistemic state.

rows.anchor: $$K_t=\Phi(\mathcal F_t,\Pi_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t,M_t,H_t)$$ ... this equation must remain **[PROP]**, not theorem. ... measure theory does **not** derive the semantic transformation Phi.
rows.statement: Defines Knowledge Construction as K_t = Phi(F_t, Pi_t, Q_t, C_t, S_t, M_t, H_t) (information, probabilistic assessment, inquiry, context, knower standpoint, model/assumptions, alternatives), explicitly held as [PROP] not theorem since measure theory does not and cannot derive the semantic transformation function Phi itself.
missing: a formal definition of the semantic construction function Phi

rows.anchor: $$P_t(A)=P(Z\in A\mid\mathcal F_t)$$ for A in A. But we must **not** write: P_t(K)=amount of knowledge. Nor: P_t(K)=truth. Nor: P_t(K)=confidence. ... Probability != Knowledge.
rows.statement: Defines Knowledge Probability P_t(A)=P(Z in A|F_t) for measurable A, while explicitly forbidding the interpretations P_t(K)=amount-of-knowledge, P_t(K)=truth, or P_t(K)=confidence -- restating Probability != Knowledge as a standing constraint on this new formal apparatus.

rows.anchor: $$I_t=I(Q_t,C_t,S_t,EC_t)$$ ... Thus I_t in K rather than necessarily I_t in X. ... Ideal Knowledge State != complete Knowledge Space. The ideal state is what is sufficient for an inquiry. It is not "everything that could possibly be known."
rows.statement: Types the Ideal Knowledge State I_t=I(Q_t,C_t,S_t,EC_t) as living in the space of admissible Knowledge States K (not necessarily in the raw configuration space X), explicitly reinforcing Ideal Knowledge State != complete Knowledge Space: the ideal state is what is sufficient for an inquiry, not everything possibly knowable.

rows.anchor: The improved definition is a typed discrepancy operator: $$\Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t;Q_t,C_t,EC_t)$$ with codomain Delta_t in G ... We should **not yet assume** that G=R. A candidate decomposition is: $$\Delta_t=(\Delta_t^{content},\Delta_t^{uncertainty},\Delta_t^{model},\Delta_t^{observability},\Delta_t^{requirement})$$
rows.statement: Replaces the invalid S_t*-K_t set-subtraction Knowledge Gap formula with a typed discrepancy operator Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t;Q_t,C_t,EC_t) whose codomain G is explicitly not assumed to be the real numbers, with a candidate five-component decomposition (content, uncertainty, model, observability, requirement) offered as [PROP].
missing: a ratified definition of the codomain G and its component structure

rows.anchor: $$Zero(K_t,I_t,EC_t)\iff K_t\models EC_t$$ or equivalently: $$Zero_t=1\iff Adequate(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t).$$ Zero is therefore a **predicate**, not a probability. ... Zero != P(A)=0.
rows.statement: Defines Zero formally as an indicator predicate: Zero(K_t,I_t,EC_t) iff K_t satisfies (models) the epistemic contract EC_t, equivalently Zero_t=1 iff Adequate(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) -- explicitly a predicate, not a probability, reinforcing Zero != P(A)=0 using the infinite-coin-toss warning against conflating point-probability-zero with epistemic absence.

rows.anchor: $$T_t:(K_t,\mathcal F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t)\longrightarrow K_{t+1}.$$ If the transition is deterministic ... If it is uncertain, define a probability kernel: $$T_t(k,A)=P(K_{t+1}\in A\mid K_t=k,\mathcal F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t).$$
rows.statement: Defines Epistemic Transition T_t either as a deterministic function (K_t,F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t) -> K_{t+1} or, if uncertain, as a probability transition kernel T_t(k,A)=P(K_{t+1} in A | K_t=k, F_t, E_{t+1}, Q_t, C_t), directly compatible with Tulcea's-theorem-style construction of an infinite process from an initial distribution and successive kernels.

rows.anchor: $$\Omega_K=\prod_{t=0}^{\infty}\mathcal X_t.$$ A trajectory is omega_K=(K_0,K_1,K_2,...). ... coordinate projection is pi_t(omega_K)=K_t. ... History != Current State. ... (Omega_K, A_K, P_K) is the **Knowledge-process probability space**. ... rather than calling Knowledge Space itself a probability space.
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge Trajectory Space Omega_K = product over t of X_t with trajectories omega_K=(K_0,K_1,...) and coordinate projections K_t=pi_t(omega_K), giving History != Current State a rigorous construction; the resulting (Omega_K, A_K, P_K), when a trajectory probability law exists, is named the Knowledge-process probability space -- the correct place for the phrase 'infinite probability space', never Knowledge Space (X,A) itself.

rows.anchor: For a knower S, define $$\mathcal F_t^S=\sigma(Y_s^S:s\le t)$$ ... F_t^A != F_t^B can hold even when A and B observe the same underlying object. Therefore: K_t^A != K_t^B does not imply that one is necessarily wrong.
rows.statement: Defines an observer-specific Epistemic Filtration F_t^S=sigma(Y_s^S : s<=t) for a knower S, giving a formal version of 'the knower's available information changes over time' and formalizing that two knowers' filtrations F_t^A != F_t^B (hence K_t^A != K_t^B) can both hold without either knower being wrong -- preserving the 'knower owns the epistemic frame' principle with mathematical structure.

rows.anchor: we need a semantic equivalence relation $$r_1\equiv_{\mathrm{sem}}r_2$$ iff they preserve the same required epistemic meaning ... if B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) is the observable epistemic behaviour of representation r, then: r1=_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain. This is not supplied by measure theory. It is the mathematical object demanded by the latest kernel experiment.
rows.statement: Defines Semantic Equivalence r1 =_sem r2 for two admissible representations of epistemic states as agreement of an observable-behaviour function B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) over the admissible test domain, explicitly noting this is NOT supplied by measure theory but is exactly the mathematical object the kernel-reduction experiment's instability demands.
missing: a concrete definition of B_r for KnowledgeOS

rows.anchor: $$X\sim_PY\iff P(X\neq Y)=0.$$ But: equiv_sem != ~_P. ... syntactic equality != representation equality != semantic equivalence != almost-sure equality.
rows.statement: Formally separates semantic equivalence (=_sem, agreement of observable behaviour) from measure-theoretic almost-sure equivalence (X ~_P Y iff P(X!=Y)=0), giving a four-way non-collapse: syntactic equality != representation equality != semantic equivalence != almost-sure equality, judged extremely important for the kernel research.

rows.anchor: This new formulation explains **why the previous 13-vs-8 kernel experiment became unstable**. The experiment was effectively asking: What is the smallest operator set? before completely fixing: X, A, =_sem, K, D, T. ... The correct research order is now: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.
rows.statement: Explains the kernel-reduction experiment's 13-vs-8 instability as a direct consequence of attempting to answer 'what is the smallest operator set' before fixing X (carrier), A (sigma-field), =_sem (semantic equivalence), K (Knowledge-State space), D (gap operator) and T (transition); prescribes a corrected nine-stage research order: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.

rows.anchor: > ### **Definition — Knowledge Space** > A **Knowledge Space** is a measurable epistemic state space $$\mathsf{KS}=(\mathcal X,\mathscr A)$$ ... Probability describes uncertainty over epistemic possibilities or trajectories; it does not by itself define semantic knowledge, truth, justification, or epistemic adequacy.
rows.statement: States the file's final, most authoritative recommended definition: a Knowledge Space is a measurable epistemic state space KS=(X,A); a current Knowledge State K_t induces a measurable compatibility region Gamma(K_t); available information is a filtration; a probability law may optionally be defined over (X,A) or over trajectories Omega_K; the resulting (Omega_K,A_K,P_K) is the Knowledge-process probability space; and probability by itself never defines semantic knowledge, truth, justification or epistemic adequacy.

rows.anchor: We have moved from: "What is Knowledge Space?" to: **What is the minimal admissible family of epistemic observables** \(\{Y_j\}_{j\in J}\) **that generates** \((\mathcal X,\mathscr A)\)? That is the **next derivation I would do before touching the kernel again**.
rows.statement: Reframes the central open research question from 'what is Knowledge Space' to 'what is the minimal admissible family of epistemic observables {Y_j} that generates (X,A)', explicitly prioritized ahead of returning to the kernel-reduction question.

rows.anchor: $$observes(a,i,t)\not\Rightarrow Knows(a,p,c,t).$$ ... Observation != Knowledge ... $$represents(i,x)$$ ... Representation != Reality and Representation != Truth. This is precisely why the previous measure-theoretic formulation was too aggressive: a point in a mathematical space would already be a representation
rows.statement: Reinforces Observation != Knowledge (observing information i does not imply Knows) and adds Representation != Reality, Representation != Truth via a represents(i,x) relation, explicitly using this to critique the earlier same-day measure-theoretic formulation as too aggressive: identifying a point in a mathematical configuration space directly with knowledge collapses the represented object into its representation.

rows.anchor: The probabilistic regime may construct (Omega,F,P) and derive: P(p|F_t)=0.93. But the core does **not** change: Knows(a,p,c,t) into: P(p|F_t)=0.93. Therefore: $$PosteriorAssessment\neq KnowledgeAttribution$$ This is one of the strongest architectural invariants we now have.
rows.statement: Worked example connecting the regime architecture to the earlier measure-theoretic apparatus: a probabilistic regime may compute P(p|F_t)=0.93 as a projection over the core, but this NEVER changes the core relation Knows(a,p,c,t) into that number -- giving PosteriorAssessment != KnowledgeAttribution as one of the strongest architectural invariants reached so far.
