sources.note: Invariant: process/session identity is evidential only; no gate reads it as an authority input.

rows.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
rows.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

rows.anchor: M4 must be classified NOT ATTESTED -- never MISSING. ... Calling it MISSING asserts "no receipt", which the evidence does not support. Calling it present asserts a binding the platform cannot make.
rows.statement: Extension of the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS discipline to condition classification: a receipt that exists but cannot be bound to its executing session (M4) must be classified NOT ATTESTED, since calling it MISSING or VALID would each assert something the platform cannot establish.
invariants: a failure to establish binding must remain unresolved rather than converted into either 'no receipt' or 'valid receipt'

rows.anchor: two residues no selection resolves ... knowledge versions K ... all three new propositions are silent on it ... S is unattestable. INV-ATTR-1 -- no gate reads identity ... E2 must mark the session-execution reference RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED.
rows.statement: Two residues survive any D1 selection unresolved: whether 'knowledge versions K' remains a required receipt property (silently dropped by all three new propositions), and that the session-execution reference S must be marked RECORDED-NOT-ATTESTED per INV-ATTR-1/D4.3's M4 finding, both flagged for E2 (receipt completeness) to settle.

rows.anchor: recording session identity != attesting session identity ... recording an applicability reference != attesting correctness of applicability
rows.statement: D3 formalises two non-equivalences carrying the decision: recording session identity is not attesting session identity, and recording an applicability reference is not attesting the correctness of applicability -- the platform cannot attest 'a specified session execution' (INV-ATTR-1/2), so identity binding is placed outside C-10's boundary entirely.

rows.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
rows.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.
invariants: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one

rows.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
rows.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

rows.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
rows.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

rows.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
rows.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

rows.anchor: you may self-bind identity; you may never self-choose role, scope, work item, or authority.
rows.statement: Restates the governing invariant for the candidate-declaration mechanism: a process may discover and declare its own runtime identity, but may never self-select the role, scope, work item, or authority it is to hold -- those must come from the authoritative commission (AST-018 next-actor), with a MISMATCH between the prompt's claimed role and the commission's role forcing STOP (GO-08).
invariants: self-bind identity only, never self-choose role/scope/work-item/authority

rows.anchor: F-3 is disclosed as aggravating, not exculpatory: producing this record adds a further participating act by 77b85fa3 on this work item. If the PO/ARB's ruling turns on 'has this process already acted here,' this record is itself part of the evidence against it.
rows.statement: A candidate for an independence-sensitive review role discloses that the very act of writing its own declaration record is itself a further participating act that could count against its own independence, explicitly refusing to treat its own record-production as exculpatory -- an instance of radical self-disclosure over self-serving interpretation.

rows.anchor: Do not decide for yourself that read-only orientation is or is not participation if the governing policy is ambiguous. Report the factual evidence. The candidate therefore returned UNDETERMINED and stopped, rather than self-certifying under reading B.
rows.statement: Establishes a governance behavioral principle: when a governing policy is deliberately left as a placeholder and genuinely ambiguous, the correct response for a self-assessing process is to report factual evidence and return UNDETERMINED rather than adjudicate the ambiguity in its own favor, escalating the open question to the PO/ARB with named legitimate dispositions instead of a recommendation.

rows.anchor: role != process identity, identity != eligibility, eligibility != appointment, appointment != activation, activation != authorization ... A process identity is DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME -- never invented by the human, copied from another session, inferred from prompt text, or chosen from a human-entered UUID.
rows.statement: Formalizes a six-link non-collapse chain of governance-identity concepts (role != process identity != eligibility != appointment != activation != authorization), each a genuinely separate step, and the rule that process identity is always discovered from the runtime, never supplied, copied, inferred, or human-chosen.

rows.anchor: Basis: PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTION -- not self-declaration. The producer never declared this identity in any governed artifact. It is attributed here by a third party from runtime evidence. ... Every prior identity in this estate was declared by the process itself. This one is attributed by a third party from evidence the producer never confirmed. That is a new act type here.
rows.statement: Introduces provenance-attributed identity as a genuinely new act type in this estate's governance model, distinct from the previously universal rule (INV-ATTR-1/2, G-2) that process identity is always self-declared and never attestable by others: here Governance attributes a producer identity to a third-party process from transcript timestamp/content evidence the producer itself never confirmed, bounded explicitly as barring-only (never enabling), evidentially grounded in operator-side transcripts outside the governed repository store, and remaining falsifiable/supersedable if contradicting evidence appears.

lineage_claims.quote: Every prior identity in this estate was declared by the process itself ... This one is attributed by a third party

experiment.hypothesis: a single identifiable session produced all AST-019 artifacts
experiment.setup: scan 65 project session transcripts for Write/Edit operations on the five AST-019 artifacts and correlate timestamps with the commit clock
experiment.method: grep governed artifacts for embedded identity (found none); cross-reference transcript write-operation timestamps against commit time; measure mention density per session as corroboration
experiment.result: exactly one session (1899d8bf) performed all Write/Edit operations across a 29-minute RED->GREEN->document->commit sequence with its single git commit landing within 2 seconds of the recorded commit time; an alternative candidate (b51dba91) discussed the slice heavily but wrote none of the artifacts
experiment.interpretation: 1899d8bf is the producer of AST-019, established by provenance rather than self-declaration

rows.anchor: Direction A -- false independence (the dangerous one; the one that actually materialised). ... Nothing malicious is required. A restart is enough. ... Direction B -- lost continuity (the tolerable one). ... The rule below deliberately errs toward Direction B. A wrongly-barred process needs one governed act to be re-established. A wrongly-admitted one cannot be repaired at all.
rows.statement: Analyzes the O-5 instability as producing two asymmetric failure directions: (A) false independence -- a restarted process presenting a clean UUID could be wrongly admitted as independent while carrying the complete prior context of the very work it should be excluded from, destroying the independence guarantee retrospectively with a record that looks clean; (B) lost continuity -- a legitimately continuing process cannot prove it is the registered lane holder and must be re-established, a merely tolerable cost. States the governing principle that any remedy must err toward B, since a wrongly-barred process is one governed act away from repair while a wrongly-admitted one can never be repaired because its check was never actually independent.
invariants: remedies must err toward false-negative (over-barring) rather than false-positive (wrongly admitting) independence

rows.statement: The independent mathematical/statistical/computational audit (GN-46) reached overall verdict MATHEMATICALLY SOUND WITH QUALIFICATIONS, found no Critical or High finding, independently reimplemented and reran EXP-01 (strengthening the interpretation of its negative result under the tested abstraction), concluded duplicate/dependency safety is a pipeline property rather than simply an aggregation-operator property, noted the standalone EXP-01 CSV remains unreliable without its generator, and found Zero(K,EC) has stronger direct source support than originally recorded. This is not to be read as proof the architecture is complete.

rows.anchor: R1 — Transformation semantics ... R2 — Identity calculus ... What does it mean for two K_t states to be equal? ... R3 — Evidence-calculus successor ... the smallest dependency-aware evidence calculus preserving the required properties
rows.statement: Three open mathematical/formal research areas are named: R1 Transformation semantics (how evidence becomes determination, how statuses transition, how proposals become decisions, how actions change state, how policy changes affect evaluation); R2 Identity calculus (what it means for two K_t states to be equal, impacting replay/deduplication/persistence/state comparison/transition testing/history -- 'Do not invent an equality definition casually'); R3 Evidence-calculus successor (goal: the smallest dependency-aware evidence calculus preserving the required properties, explicitly a research problem, not a book-writing exercise).

rows.statement: Summary of selected GN-46 mathematical-verification findings: MV-F-5 (no ratified admissibility law exactly matches the six-tuple Decision Contract); MV-F-6 (the Proposal->Decision edge contains an unstated lift, e.g. d:=adopt(a), currently classified as modelling omission/formal incompleteness, not a demonstrated architectural contradiction); MV-F-7 (in-force policy uniqueness under multiple authorities is not established); MV-F-8/9/10 (missing formal semantics around Zero<->Evidence typing, policy-stratification base case, governed handling of CONFLICTED); MV-F-22 (K_t equality remains undefined). Governing formulation: 'No demonstrated contradiction or invariant violation; several formal under-specifications remain' -- not to be replaced by either a weaker or stronger restatement.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Answer to the governing question: BOTH.** The synthesis mostly performed deliberate abstraction (8+ members defensible) — AND it demonstrably discarded five load-bearing pieces (PF-1-triple, Γ, Q, the d-producer, the governance algebra's uniqueness/escalation core)
rationale_evidence.statement: Applying a mandated 6-step compression-family test to each PF member individually (source form, ratified form, what was removed, whether the removal was explained, what ratified property is affected, and the resulting classification), the governing question of whether the source-to-ratified-synthesis compression was deliberate abstraction or loss is answered BOTH: the synthesis mostly performed deliberate, defensible abstraction (8+ members judged defensible with no affected ratified property identified, e.g. PF-5b's operational Zero intentionally held open by OQ-4, PF-6's branches re-homed by a ratified decision D-FA-1, AF-F-11's dropped selector context argument), AND it demonstrably discarded five load-bearing pieces whose absence leaves ratified transitions under-typed: the PF-1 triple (Insufficient/Stale/Prohibited), Gamma (sufficiency rules, PF-5a), Q (epistemic sufficiency, PF-7), the decision-producing 'd-producer' (PF-8's MV-F-6 sliver), and the governance algebra's uniqueness/escalation core (PF-9). Not one of the five breaks a ratified invariant today; each limits the evaluability or expressibility of a ratified element.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 1 **Source-to-synthesis compression** ... 2 **Transformation semantics under-specified** ... 3 **Identity/equality semantics** ... 4 **Authorization/governance resolution semantics** ... 5 **L2→L3/L4 realization gap**
rationale_evidence.statement: All 27 underlying findings are consolidated into five systemic themes, each with a diagnosed root cause: (1) source-to-synthesis compression -- root: ratification recorded selections without loss-ledgers, part architectural (5 load-bearing members) and part merely explanatory; (2) transformation semantics under-specified (eta, ladder transition calculus, policy dynamics plus genesis, action semantics, adjudication, Learn/F) -- one root: the corpus formalized states/structures/boundaries but never the transformations between them, classified research; (3) identity/equality semantics (evidence equivalence, frame equivalence, requirement identity, K_t equality) -- one root: no identity calculus exists, classified research, with I-5 and replay conditionally defined until it does; (4) authorization/governance resolution semantics (the PF-9 governance-algebra core plus un-ratified escalation/AI-non-override plus AF-F-15's adjudication gap) -- one root: L5 (practice-layer) governance is richer than L2's (ratified-layer) governance surface, classified architectural-candidate; (5) the L2-to-L3/L4 realization gap -- standing and honest, no new members, characterized as a conformance profile rather than a defect.

rationale_evidence.anchor: measure theory; probability; entropy; KL divergence; Wasserstein/epistemic distance; topology; knowledge-density/flux; knowledge-space Ω; continuous evolution equations ... $$\frac{\partial k}{\partial t}+\nabla\cdot J=S-D$$
rationale_evidence.statement: Documents that the earlier historical KnowledgeOS work explored a much broader range of mathematical frameworks than the current v0.2 architecture retains: measure theory, probability, entropy, KL divergence, Wasserstein/epistemic distance, topology, knowledge-density/flux, a knowledge-space Omega, and continuous evolution equations -- for example a proposed continuity-style PDE, partial(k)/partial(t) + div(J) = S - D, with quantities like coverage, uncertainty, information gain, stability, and epistemic distance. States that later falsification/archaeology correctly concluded these should not automatically become the KnowledgeOS mathematical foundation, and explicitly frames the current mathematical audit (GN-46, S1326) as doing exactly this same separation work: distinguishing interesting mathematical frameworks from mathematics actually established by the ratified architecture -- consistent with GN-46's own finding that no metric/measure/entropy/topology claim appears anywhere in the ratified material.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The model is ready for experiment, not proven theory. ... The current architecture findings: transformation semantics; K_t equality; evidence aggregation; policy dynamics; Proposal→Decision lift; computability; are therefore **not completely new problems**. They are later, more rigorous manifestations of questions the earlier Step work was already discovering.
rationale_evidence.statement: The earlier Step-era handover to the executable phase stated, in substance, 'the model is ready for experiment, not proven theory', and explicitly marked as unresolved: the exact KnowledgeState algebra, the exact Evidence algebra, exact statistical inference, an exact causal framework, exact ontology, aggregate boundaries, persistence, and production technology. This document argues that the current architecture findings -- transformation semantics, K_t equality, evidence aggregation, policy dynamics, the Proposal-to-Decision lift, and computability (all findings registered in this batch's S1326/S1329/S1334) -- are therefore not completely new problems, but later, more rigorous manifestations of questions the earlier Step-era work had already discovered were open.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Early conceptual model ↓ KnowledgeState / lenses / journey ↓ Sārathi + Zero + Lord separation ↓ "Before we continue" / objective revision ↓ formal Questions ↓ 25-series formalization ↓ Step 049 kernel reduction ↓ Step 050 adversarial audit ↓ falsification ↓ v0.2 canonical synthesis ↓ Final Architecture ↓ mathematical re-audit
rationale_evidence.statement: Sketches a twelve-stage historical evolution pipeline: early conceptual model -> KnowledgeState/lenses/journey -> Sarathi+Zero+Lord separation -> 'before we continue'/objective revision -> formal Questions -> the 25-series formalization -> Step 049 kernel reduction -> Step 050 adversarial audit -> falsification -> v0.2 canonical synthesis -> Final Architecture -> the current mathematical re-audit (GN-46, S1326). Characterizes v0.2 as a compression and purification of a much larger body of theory, explaining why current Edition-2 production is finding exactly the gaps it is finding. Recommends, rather than reconstructing artificial Step numbers beyond 156, building a four-way crosswalk: Step-era theory <-> v0.2 formal model <-> mathematical research <-> Gita Chapters 1-4, which would show which ideas were already discovered, formally retained, compressed, left open, rediscovered philosophically, and are now testable mathematically -- framed as a much stronger intellectual history of KnowledgeOS than simply claiming the Gita inspired the architecture. Poses an unresolved open research question: what mathematical object is actually produced by epistemic discernment -- a single action a_t in A, a three-valued classification D(K_t,G,Policy) -> {Permitted, Forbidden, Undetermined} over candidate actions, or a map D: A -> {epistemically justified classes}? Explicitly states this is not yet known.

sources.note: A verification phase/principle requiring every KnowledgeOS core primitive to have an explicit observable input space, output space, and finite computational procedure (possibly nondeterministic); classifies operations as deterministic/probabilistic/policy-dependent/human-authoritative and proposes a ten-question realizability audit per primitive.

rows.anchor: \forall F\in\mathcal F_{\text{core}}, \quad F\text{ is formally defined} \land F\text{ is computable} \land F\text{ has an observable input}
rows.statement: Introduces the Computational Realizability Principle as a new verification phase: for every core primitive operation, it must be formally defined, computable, and have an observable input. Computable ≠ Perfect — KnowledgeOS does not need perfect observation/parsing/inference, only the ability to represent what it observed, how, how reliably, and what remains unknown. Formal statement: ∀f∈F_core there exist an observable input space X_f, an output space Y_f, and f:X_f->Y_f implementable by a finite computational procedure, possibly with explicitly represented uncertainty or nondeterminism.

rows.anchor: SemanticParse \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
rows.statement: Walks 14 core primitives (Receive Intent, Structural Parse, Semantic Reconstruction, Dimension Discovery, Acquire Evidence, Create Observation, Create Assertion, Coherence Checking, Conflict Detection, Gap Detection, Discrepancy, Distance, Sārathi Navigation, Lord) through a computability check, each judged computable but with varying determinism. Notably SemanticParse->CandidateMeaning, not SemanticParse->Truth (semantic parsing is probabilistic, not a deterministic oracle), and Candidate ≠ Knowledge for Lord's outputs. Coherence/Conflict/Gap detection are judged deterministic PROVIDED the relevant rules/Ideal-State are made explicit (e.g. conflict example: two Nexus-version assertions on the same entity/dimension/context/validity interval trigger a deterministic 'potential contradiction' flag, without the system knowing which is true).

rows.anchor:
Deterministic

Schema validation
Type checking
rows.statement: Classifies KnowledgeOS operations into four categories: Deterministic (schema validation, type checking, set/temporal comparison, conflict rule evaluation, gap calculation, hashing, provenance linkage); Probabilistic (language interpretation, semantic reconstruction, entity resolution, classification, candidate generation, inference); Policy-dependent (severity, adequacy, ideal-state selection, prioritization, resolution strategy); Human-authoritative (decisions intentionally requiring human approval — 'not a failure of KnowledgeOS, a governance boundary'). Also shows an LLM can participate in KnowledgeOS (as Parser/LLM/Database feeding Evidence->Observation->Knowledge) without becoming KnowledgeOS: the LLM performs semantic interpretation/candidate/hypothesis generation/summarization/reasoning assistance, while KnowledgeOS retains control of identity, provenance, evidence, state, epistemic status, coherence, conflicts, gaps, transitions, governance.

rows.anchor: Question 19A — Computational Realizability of KnowledgeOS
rows.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical expansion (before Questions 20+) to insert Question 19A — Computational Realizability of KnowledgeOS: for every primitive, answer (1) what is the input, (2) can it be observed/acquired, (3) what algorithm/process computes it, (4) what is the output, (5) deterministic/probabilistic/policy-dependent?, (6) what uncertainty is preserved, (7) what evidence/provenance is attached, (8) what happens on computation failure, (9) can the result be reproduced, (10) can another KnowledgeOS instance verify it. Answering these for every primitive would give 'the beginnings of an executable mathematical specification for KnowledgeOS' — proposed as the correct next milestone before 'closing the theory'.

rows.anchor: Observation = Acquired\ information\ through\ a\ defined\ observation\ channel
rows.statement: Resolves the earlier worry that Observation might not be computable: Observation is not restricted to sensors — it can come from a database query, document extraction, web retrieval, a human statement, or a runtime API result, each shown as a channel->artifact->Observation pipeline. Formalizes Observe:(Source,AcquisitionMethod,Artifact,Context,Time)->Observation, implementable via ordinary technology (parsers, DB drivers, HTTP clients, APIs, filesystem/Git access, OCR, speech-to-text, structured parsers, LLMs, rule engines, human input interfaces) — 'Observation is computationally realizable.'

type_signature.domain: source x acquisition method x artifact x context x time

rows.anchor: L1 — Conceptual definition ... L2 — Mathematical specification ... L3 — Computable semantics
rows.statement: Classifies theory maturity into three levels: L1 Conceptual definition (know what a thing means, mostly resolved), L2 Mathematical specification (can define inputs/outputs/invariants, mostly resolved), L3 Computable semantics (know an executable algorithm producing the result, NOT completely resolved) — the theory has reached L2 for most of the architecture but not L3 everywhere.

rows.anchor: Observe ... Interpret ... DiscoverDimensions ... AssessEvidence ... DetectConflict ... EvaluateCoherence ... ConstructIdeal ... MeasureDiscrepancy
rows.statement: Names eight operators still requiring computational closure, each individually diagnosed: Observe(x,C) (what makes a database row / human statement / LLM output / sensor reading count as an observation, still unformalized); semantic reconstruction f_semantic:Text×Context->SemanticRepresentation (unspecified, needed to detect when a question is insufficiently specified and generate clarification); DiscoverDimensions (needs an acceptance criterion for when a candidate dimension is sufficiently justified to enter the Knowledge Model); AssessEvidence(E,A,C)->(Support,Uncertainty,Validity) (needs to account for source reliability, relevance, independence, corroboration, contradiction, temporal validity, provenance, having rejected Support=Probability); DetectConflict (ConflictDetection=RuleEvaluation, needing SameSubject∧SameDimension∧CompatibleScope∧TemporalOverlap∧IncompatibleValues, with the rule language/semantics unspecified); EvaluateCoherence (Coherent(K)=W∧L∧E∧T∧C is defined but each predicate like Logical(K) or Contextual(K) still needs an executable validator); ConstructIdeal (needs an Ideal-State authority model — who determines what is desired: Human/Constitution/Policy/Domain rules/Purpose/Manifesto/ADR/System configuration/LLM proposal/Negotiation — otherwise KnowledgeOS could manufacture an unauthorized 'ideal'); MeasureDiscrepancy (Δ≠necessarily one scalar is settled, but numeric d(x,y)=|x-y| vs categorical d(Confirmed,Observed) vs understanding-distance d(U_1,U_2) may not even be a metric, favoring 'Typed Discrepancy' over one universal distance function).
missing: formal algorithms for all eight operators

rows.anchor: Deterministic\ Kernel + Explicit\ Policy + Probabilistic/AI\ Proposals + Human\ Authority
rows.statement: Distinguishes three computational classes: Class A Deterministic (schema, types, relations, temporal/logical rules, provenance, state transitions, constraint checking, hashing, identity — machine-verifiable); Class B Policy-governed (evidence sufficiency, severity, relevance, ideal-state requirements, conflict policies, acceptance thresholds — explicit policies, not mathematical truths); Class C Generative/interpretive (semantic parsing, dimension discovery, hypothesis/question generation, interpretation, horizon expansion — AI/LLM output enters as Candidate, never automatically as Truth). Resulting architecture: Deterministic Kernel + Explicit Policy + Probabilistic/AI Proposals + Human Authority, rather than pretending everything is mathematically objective.

rows.anchor: Every unresolved computation has an identifiable boundary.
rows.statement: Final verdict: not 'the complete mathematical model is finished' but 'the conceptual and structural mathematical model is substantially complete, but the operational semantics of several epistemic operators remain to be formally specified' — none of the eight named operators is an 'undefined philosophical black hole' any more; every unresolved computation has an identifiable boundary. Recommends a 'KnowledgeOS Computational Closure' phase: for every operator specify Domain->Input Types->Preconditions->Algorithm->Output Type->Invariants->Failure Modes, tested against concrete examples (Arjuna/Gita, Nexus infrastructure, software architecture, ADRs, databases, internet sources, LLM outputs, human instructions), giving the chain Theory->Formal Model->Computational Model->Executable KnowledgeOS as the point at which implementation may responsibly begin.

rows.anchor: LLM: Observation \rightarrow Interpretation
rows.statement: Shows exactly where the LLM fits without bypassing the epistemic boundary: LLM:Observation->Interpretation, or LLM:Question->CandidateDimensions, or LLM:KnowledgeState->CandidateHypothesis; every LLM output flows through KnowledgeOS rules and is either Accepted or Rejected before reaching the Knowledge State — 'one of the most important architectural properties of KnowledgeOS'. Per-operator computability check: Observe (yes, via database query/HTTP response/file read/human statement/LLM response/sensor); Interpret (yes but heterogeneous — parser/ontology/rules/LLM/human interpretation, result always a candidate); Assess (yes if policies explicit); Construct Assertion (yes); Update Knowledge State (yes).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Acquisition Closure
rows.statement: States the 'KnowledgeOS Acquisition Closure' result: every admissible information source can be transformed into a provenance-bearing artifact, observed through an explicit acquisition operation, interpreted into candidate semantic objects, epistemically assessed, and (if accepted under governing rules) incorporated into the Knowledge State — stronger than 'KnowledgeOS can read documents'. But flags Interpretation as still only architecturally, not fully computationally, closed: must handle unstructured text, incomplete questions, ambiguity, multiple possible interpretations, domain-specific meaning, implicit dimensions, contradictory interpretations, and LLM-generated interpretations — proposing 'Computational Closure 1 — Observation' then 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation and Dimension Discovery' as the next concrete steps in place of proceeding to Question 21.

rows.anchor: ARCHITECTURALLY CLOSED, SEMANTICALLY OPEN
rows.statement: Declares Source Observation CLOSED and Interpretation 'ARCHITECTURALLY CLOSED, SEMANTICALLY OPEN' — we know how the operation works structurally, but the interpretation content may legitimately remain ambiguous, incomplete, multiple, AI-assisted, human-assisted, or domain-dependent, which is 'not a defect'; forcing interpretation to be deterministic would damage the model. Proposes a Semantic Reconstruction bounded context owning SemanticInterpretation/CandidateDimension/CandidateEntity/CandidateRelationship/CandidateProposition/Ambiguity/InterpretationMethod/InterpretationEvidence but explicitly NOT owning truth, final epistemic status, domain authority, or governance decisions.

rows.anchor: Input → Artifact | Closed ... Assertion ↔ Gap | Needs gap detector formalization
rows.statement: Nine-row closure-status table: Input->Artifact (Closed), Artifact->SourceObservation (Closed), SourceObservation->Interpretation (architecturally closed, interpretation can be ambiguous), Interpretation->CandidateProposition (Closed), CandidateProposition->Assertion (closed conceptually, admission policy remains configurable), Assertion->KnowledgeState (Closed), Assertion<->Evidence (needs formal evidence model), Assertion<->Conflict (needs conflict-rule formalization), Assertion<->Gap (needs gap-detector formalization). Names 'Evidence' as the next major closure target: what counts as evidence, how it relates to an assertion, how it can be computationally evaluated without reducing epistemic reasoning to an arbitrary confidence score, to be tested against direct measurement/DB output/document statement/human testimony/expert opinion/LLM output/derived calculation/multiple independent sources/circular sources/stale sources/contradictory sources, aiming to make Assess(A,E,Π,C)->Σ_A 'computationally realizable rather than merely philosophical'.

rows.anchor: Computability boundary: undecidability, three distinct failure modes, and the Unknown/Uncomputable/Intractable distinction
rows.statement: Notes simple graph/temporal/provenance queries and deterministic invariant checks are cheaply computable (e.g. O(V+E), O(1)), but reachability/state-explosion can be intractable (n binary variables give |S|=2^n, e.g. 2^100 for n=100, not enumerable), mitigated by abstraction/symbolic reasoning/compositional verification (linking back to Step 48). Statistical operations (mean, variance, regression, Bayesian updating, hypothesis testing) are generally feasible; causal inference has no single complexity class (combinatorial search, latent variables, model uncertainty, missing data); decision optimization can become NP-hard. States a fundamental computability limitation: some questions about arbitrary programs (e.g. halting) are undecidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise UniversalVerification and must support Unknown as a legitimate final result. Strengthens Step 41's Unknown by adding Uncomputable and Intractable as distinct categories, and separates three non-conflatable failure modes: epistemic failure (InsufficientEvidence), computational failure (CannotComputeWithinBudget), and mathematical limitation (Undecidable).
invariants: epistemic failure, computational failure, and mathematical undecidability are never conflated

lineage_claims.quote: This strengthens Step 41.

rows.anchor: Computational budget, graceful degradation with mandatory status preservation, ComputeResult contract with error bounds
rows.statement: Defines Budget=(Time,Memory,Cost) and Compute(f,Budget) returning ExactResult, Approximation, or Unresolved. Requires graceful degradation Exact -> Approximate -> Heuristic -> Unknown while the system 'must preserve the status' -- explicitly forbidding silent approximation (ExactFailure -> Guess presented as fact); instead ApproximationUsed=True must be recorded. Defines a formal computational contract ComputeResult = (Value, Method, Status, ErrorBound, Cost) (example: Value=tau-hat, Method=MonteCarlo, Status=Approximate, ErrorBound=epsilon) -- 'mathematically much stronger than returning only a number' -- and requires an error bound |x-hat - x|<=epsilon be reported only when meaningful, never invented. Also classifies ReasoningMode in {Formal, Deterministic, Statistical, Probabilistic, Heuristic, LLMGenerated}, each with different assurance characteristics; an LLM-generated conclusion is CandidateInference, not automatically equivalent to FormalInference -- 'this preserves our epistemic firewall'.
invariants: approximation is always explicitly flagged (ApproximationUsed=True), never presented silently as an exact result
an error bound is reported only when genuinely meaningful, never invented

rows.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 49 primitive-reduction model (all PASS)
rows.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) can Evidence exist without Observation? No => Evidence is derived; (2) can Provenance exist without Relations? No => Provenance is relational structure; (3) can Causality be represented as generic RelatedTo? Not safely => Causes must be a typed relation; (4) can Learning be represented as a static object? Not adequately => it is a transition K_t->K_{t+1}; (5) can Decision be separated from Action? Yes => Decision->Action, preserving authorization/dry-run semantics; (6) can Outcome be treated as Decision? No => an outcome is a post-action observation; (7) can Unknown be represented as False? No => the three-valued epistemic distinction remains necessary; (8) can approximate computation be represented as exact? No => computation status must be retained; (9) can every theoretical KnowledgeOS question be computed exactly? No => undecidability/complexity impose limits; (10) does mathematical complexity require special hardware? Not necessarily => complexity determines resource requirements, not model validity; (11) can the same domain model run on local or distributed infrastructure? Yes, if ports/contracts isolate infrastructure; (12) can a new concept be added without increasing the primitive kernel? Yes, if derivable from existing primitives.

experiment.hypothesis: The candidate primitive kernel P={Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action} is sufficient to derive every other Step-42-48 concept, and the resulting model's computability properties are correctly characterized.
experiment.setup: Twelve discrete yes/no derivability and computability questions (49.78-49.89).
experiment.assumptions: The reduction/derivation mappings given in 49.1-49.77 of the same file are assumed correct.
experiment.inputs: Twelve scenario questions as listed in the statement field.
experiment.method: For each question, derive the expected yes/no answer from the kernel/derivation model and compare to the stated expectation.
experiment.interpretation: Step 49 reduces the architecture rather than adding to it -- a 'particularly important PASS'.
experiment.limitations: Falsification is by manual scenario reasoning within the document, not an executed/automated test suite.

rows.anchor: Three execution classes (deterministic/statistical/AI) behind a ComputePort; no infrastructure leakage into the domain
rows.statement: Introduces a statistical Result=(Estimate,Method,ModelVersion,Uncertainty,Status) type (e.g. mu-hat=12.4, CI95%=[11.7,13.1], interval preserved, no false precision beyond what the measurement supports) and reiterates Status in {Exact,Approximate,Simulation,Heuristic,Unresolved}. States the reference implementation's core computation is intentionally modest (CoreComputation << ExternalSpecializedComputation), giving DeterministicCore + PluggableCompute across three execution classes: Class A deterministic domain computation (runs locally), Class B statistical computation (local or via compute adapter), Class C AI inference (external/local model provider) -- all returning governed results through a ComputePort: Input -> ComputedResult, implementable as LocalPython/Java/RemoteService while the domain remains independent (no 'if kubernetes/postgres/openai/claude' branching inside the domain).

lineage_claims.quote: ComputePort: Input → ComputedResult.

rows.anchor: Three-boundary hierarchy Observable→Identifiable→Computable (none reversible); refines the normal-PC question
rows.statement: States Computable != Observable (easy to compute but impossible to observe from available data), Observable != Identifiable (observed variables may still lack enough information to identify a causal/statistical quantity), and Identifiable != ComputationallyCheap (an identified problem can still be computationally expensive) -- giving the three-boundary hierarchy Observable -> Identifiable -> Computable, none of the implications automatically reversible. States this directly refines the recurring 'runs on a normal PC' question: cheap computability does not make an answer epistemically valid, and a theoretically identifiable problem may need a cluster to compute efficiently -- hardware capacity is only one dimension. Experiment 12: two states producing identical (trivially computable) observations remain NotIdentifiable -- PASS. Experiment 13: a large but theoretically identifiable inference problem returns Identified=True with ComputationalCost=High -- PASS. Defines the resulting layered boundary Reality -Observation-> ObservableWorld -Inference-> IdentifiedKnowledge -Computation-> DecisionSupport, 'prevents category errors'.

lineage_claims.quote: This directly addresses the normal PC question.

rows.anchor: Normal-PC feasibility for core operations; example complexity (graph traversal, indexed lookup); provenance-lookup experiment
rows.statement: Lists operations a normal modern PC can execute: GraphTraversal, SchemaValidation, TypeChecking, ProvenanceChecking, HashVerification, EventProcessing, RuleEvaluation, ModerateStatisticalAnalysis -- 'not inherently distributed'. Gives example complexity O(V+E) for graph traversal (e.g. V=1,000,000, E=5,000,000, manageable on a single machine with engineering optimization) and O(log n) or near-constant indexed lookups (e.g. find EvidenceByClaimId). Experiment 4: retrieving all direct evidence references for a claim is a Finite Query -- PASS.

lineage_claims.quote: A normal modern PC can easily execute: GraphTraversal ... These are not inherently distributed computations.

rationale_evidence.statement: Nine-row closure-status table: Input->Artifact (Closed), Artifact->SourceObservation (Closed), SourceObservation->Interpretation (architecturally closed, interpretation can be ambiguous), Interpretation->CandidateProposition (Closed), CandidateProposition->Assertion (closed conceptually, admission policy remains configurable), Assertion->KnowledgeState (Closed), Assertion<->Evidence (needs formal evidence model), Assertion<->Conflict (needs conflict-rule formalization), Assertion<->Gap (needs gap-detector formalization). Names 'Evidence' as the next major closure target: what counts as evidence, how it relates to an assertion, how it can be computationally evaluated without reducing epistemic reasoning to an arbitrary confidence score, to be tested against direct measurement/DB output/document statement/human testimony/expert opinion/LLM output/derived calculation/multiple independent sources/circular sources/stale sources/contradictory sources, aiming to make Assess(A,E,Π,C)->Σ_A 'computationally realizable rather than merely philosophical'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Normal-PC feasibility for core operations; example complexity (graph traversal, indexed lookup); provenance-lookup experiment
rationale_evidence.statement: Lists operations a normal modern PC can execute: GraphTraversal, SchemaValidation, TypeChecking, ProvenanceChecking, HashVerification, EventProcessing, RuleEvaluation, ModerateStatisticalAnalysis -- 'not inherently distributed'. Gives example complexity O(V+E) for graph traversal (e.g. V=1,000,000, E=5,000,000, manageable on a single machine with engineering optimization) and O(log n) or near-constant indexed lookups (e.g. find EvidenceByClaimId). sources.note: Applies DDD separation of concerns (Question/Claim/Evidence/Challenge/Determination/Revision bounded contexts) to locate Knowledge Sunya as the absence of context-independent determination (Status(C)=f(C,Q,Context,E,Standards,t), never f(C) alone), not an empty claim object. Fixes a Knowledge Sunya triangle (Object emptiness/Determination emptiness/Relational emptiness, non-equivalent), identifies Sunya as a boundary concept appearing where an inter-context inference (Evidence.supports -> Determination.justified -> Governance.accepted -> True) is not explicitly established, restructures K_t into seven relational components, inserts Sunya as an intermediate transitional stage in the purification cycle (Determination->Challenge->Sunya->Revision->New Determination), and formalizes hypothesis H-SUNYA-01 (Relational Epistemic Emptiness) with its required non-implications.

rows.statement: Poses the central question of where 'sunya' appears once a knowledge system's concerns are DDD-separated, answering that Knowledge Sunya is the absence of inherent, context-independent determination -- no knowledge claim is self-sufficiently determined outside the relations that give it meaning -- not that knowledge is nothing.

rows.statement: Applies DDD separation of concerns to a knowledge system, defining six bounded contexts (Question, Claim, Evidence, Challenge, Determination, Revision) each with a distinct responsibility, preventing the conflation of claim, truth, evidence, determination, and knowledge into one object.

rows.statement: Clarifies that Knowledge Sunya does not mean the claim object is empty, but rather that a claim is not equivalent to knowledge and not equivalent to determination -- a claim by itself does not carry its complete epistemic status, which requires relations to other contexts.

rows.statement: Argues, via three worked removals (Claim minus Question, minus Evidence, minus Context), that Sunya occurs not in the object itself but in a missing relation: removing the question can erase epistemic determination, removing evidence can erase justification, and removing context can erase applicability, even though the claim syntactically persists.

sources.note: The Sat_c Semantic Closure Experiment: specifying (not implementing) the eight Sat_c classes already exposes that only 3 of 8 (content, evidence, provenance) are executable -- status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational are blocked by named missing evaluators (A-1) -- and that no class in the family requires factivity at all, so a state can satisfy all eight and still be false (A-2), locating CE-1's cause in the satisfaction family's structure rather than in Gamma. Adversarial testing then finds Sat_content is not total under contradiction (PB-2), the declared U-reason vocabulary is incomplete (PB-3), blocked-class contagion makes every composite requirement of arity>=4 permanently U (PB-4), and operational satisfaction is not provably well-founded (PB-5). Introduces a fourth Zero reading, Zero_reasoned (closes on non-agent-remediable U only), and the derived chain Zero_strict => Zero_reasoned => Zero_weak.

rows.anchor: U ├── epistemic U ... ├── theory U ├── NO_EVALUATOR ├── NO_ORDERING ... └── world U └── UNOBSERVABLE ... That is potentially more important than the eight classes themselves.
rows.statement: Proposes a three-branch taxonomy of the value U itself -- epistemic U (agent doesn't know), theory U (no evaluator exists), world U (unobservable) -- judged potentially more important than the eight requirement classes.

rows.anchor: the satisfaction family has no place to attach truth. ... If KnowledgeOS intends satisfaction to support a truth-bearing notion of knowledge, the current satisfaction family contains no semantic attachment point for that relation.
rows.statement: Endorses A-2 as the strongest finding of the run, restating it more precisely: the defect is structural (no attachment point for truth in the satisfaction family), not an accident of any particular evaluator.

rows.anchor: PB-4 is probably the most important operational result ... more requirements -> more class evaluations -> more opportunities for blocked evaluation -> U propagation -> closure becomes impossible. ... Kleene conjunction faithfully exposes semantic incompleteness.
rows.statement: Reframes PB-4 (blocked-class contagion) as evidence that Kleene conjunction is working correctly by faithfully propagating unresolved semantics, not as a defect of the composition rule.

rows.anchor: I would rename the next experiment: Sat_c Specification Repair & Evaluator Completion Experiment ... Gate 1 -- Repair, without implementation ... Gate 5 -- Ask the decisive question
rows.statement: Recommends a five-gate 'Sat_c Specification Repair & Evaluator Completion Experiment' sequencing PB-2/PB-3/PB-5 repair before candidate governance/temporal/operational evaluators are introduced, keeping the eventual Zero choice a theory/governance decision.

rows.anchor: Only 3 of 8 classes are executable now ... status | Contr undefined; whether contradiction needs a 4th value is OPEN ... governance | no evaluator exists -- this is why every governance requirement read U in E1
rows.statement: A-1: specifying (not implementing) the eight Sat_c classes reveals only 3 (content, evidence, provenance) are executable; status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational are each blocked by a named specific missing evaluator or undefined relation, explaining why E1 produced permanent U for those classes.

rows.anchor: No class in the family requires factivity. ... A knowledge state can satisfy all eight classes and still be false. CE-1 is therefore not an accident of Gamma: the satisfaction family has no place to attach truth.
rows.statement: A-2: none of the eight satisfaction classes carries any factivity requirement, so full satisfaction never entails truth -- a stronger, specification-level restatement of CE-1's mechanism.

rows.anchor: Sat_content returns top if p in Content(K) and bot if not-p in Content(K). Both can hold. The codomain {top,bot,U} has no value for it, so Sat_content is not a function on such states.
rows.statement: PB-2: Sat_content is not total under contradiction (both p and not-p present), since the codomain has no value for that case; three repairs are possible but none is chosen.

rows.anchor: blocked-class contagion: the decisive result. Every composite requirement of arity >= 4 is permanently U, no matter how well the executable classes perform.
rows.statement: PB-4: under Kleene conjunction with 5 of 8 classes blocked, every composite requirement of arity 4 or higher is permanently U, making the satisfaction family effectively inert for realistic multi-class requirements.

rows.anchor: Zero closure holds on a state whose knowledge is false. ... Zero_weak = true, Zero_reasoned = true. Because no Sat_c requires factivity (A-2). ... Zero and truth are orthogonal.
rows.statement: C-3: the B1 factivity counterexample case is nevertheless declared closed under both Zero_weak and Zero_reasoned, establishing that epistemic closure and truth are orthogonal under the current candidate semantics.

rows.anchor: Sat_c family is not semantically closed ... Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U} remains a research-level candidate interface, not a canonical semantic contract.
rows.statement: Confirms and restates the verdict that the Sat_c family is not semantically closed, keeping Sat a research-level candidate interface.

rows.anchor: Zero does not imply truth. B1 has: false attribution, Zero_weak = true, Zero_reasoned = true. Therefore: Zero !=> Truth under the current theory. ... It separates: closure != truth
rows.statement: Restates the Zero-does-not-imply-truth counterexample (B1) as probably the most important conceptual result of the experiment, separating closure from truth.

rows.anchor: (K_t, r, Gamma_t) --Eval_c--> EVal_c ... and we are explicitly not yet deciding what an evaluation value fundamentally is. ... H-EVAL-01 [PROP] ... V = {top,bot,U}
rows.statement: Pivots the research object one level below Sat to Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal, registers hypothesis H-EVAL-01 (a requirement-relative evaluation mechanism preserving explanatory structure), and recommends discovering the value codomain experimentally rather than presupposing three values.

rows.anchor: M-4. The Zero chain is derived. Zero_strict ⇒ Zero_reasoned ⇒ Zero_weak, proved in two lines and machine-checked over 1 620 000 assignments ... 0 counterexamples. It is independent of the reason partition.
rows.statement: M-4: the derived implication chain Zero_strict => Zero_reasoned => Zero_weak was proved in two lines and machine-checked over 1,620,000 assignments (every choice of which reason-buckets close) with zero counterexamples, and is independent of the reason partition even though that partition has already been revised twice.

rows.anchor: > `[EXP]` **Three-valued `Sat` makes v1.1's sentence "`Zero ⟺ Δ_t = ∅`" ambiguous: it names three predicates, and they disagree on the best case**
rows.statement: Restates the v1.2 headline one-line result: three-valued Sat makes 'Zero iff Delta_t=empty' ambiguous, naming three predicates (Zero_strict, Zero_weak, Kleene) that disagree even on the best case (a determined, corroborated state is strict=false, weak=true, Kleene=U); Theory status B (partially executable); the three undetermined requirement classes (governance, temporal, operational) are exactly the classes v1.2 marks open.

rows.statement: Maps the explicit/implicit belief distinction directly onto Sat(K_t,r) iff K_t entails Content(r), and Zero onto a complete-and-consistent ('vivid') knowledge base under the closed-world assumption -- this identification is in unreconciled tension with the main research lane's actual v1.2 finding that Sat is semantically incoherent under the theory's own model, with only 3 of 8 Sat_c classes executable.

rows.statement: Explicitly REJECTS ten over-strong translations from the Brachman & Levesque source, most notably Sat=FOL-entailment (too strong, evaluation has more dimensions) and Zero=CWA (contradicts Unknown≠Absent and NoEvidence≠EvidenceOfAbsence) -- this directly corrects the immediately preceding extraction in the same thread (S2517), which had proposed exactly these two identifications as confirmations of KnowledgeOS concepts; also rejects Zero=Delta-empty-universally (different requirement universes produce different meanings), Boundary=FrameAxiom, delta=SituationCalculus, Identity=UniqueNames+DomainClosure, DL=BoundaryTaxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL as the representation language, and flat YES/NO/UNKNOWN evaluation (already refuted by the Contr research).

sources.note: Recurring, PO/ARB-endorsed pattern: a candidate/appointed actor lacking a governed REGISTER→HANDOFF→human-START lane (or identity-barred) must refuse to act and produce only a gate-refusal report rather than invent a lane or self-authorize; recorded at least 8 times across two work items in this batch and each time explicitly ratified as 'correct behaviour, not a defect.'

rows.anchor: the candidate must not start correcting anything before the REGISTER/HANDOFF/Human START sequence exists
rows.statement: An appointed actor's own authorized_to_act must remain false, and no correction work may begin, until Governance has recorded REGISTER, HANDOFF, and a human START on the authoritative workflow record — appointment alone confers no authorization.

rows.anchor: the author must not independently review its own correction (producer bar); the author reports CORRECTED / READY FOR INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION — never ACCEPTED/ADOPTED/CLOSED
rows.statement: The Session Completion Report template (status/completed_work/evidence/open_items/next_actor/authorization) is applied to record the correction as delivered-but-not-accepted, explicitly distinguishing capability from authorization (F1) and naming the next actor as a fresh independent verifier under the producer bar (EP-02/R-34).

rows.anchor: the commissioned falsification of V-1 / V-3 / V-5 ... no REGISTER with role = verification exists in the record. No transition references this process (8deac5de).
rows.statement: A candidate verifier reads the authoritative workflow record (3 transitions, all architecture-lane) and the full 19-record census, finds no verification lane anywhere attributable to itself, runs AST-017's own bootstrap (UNRESOLVED, authorized_to_act=false, next actor governance), and on that basis refuses to perform the commissioned technical review rather than invent a lane.

rows.anchor: the record is the authority, not the instruction text (the commissioning prompt itself instructs: 'Do NOT trust this prompt alone. Read the authoritative workflow record before acting.')
rows.statement: A prompt asserting that a governed lane exists cannot substitute for the authoritative workflow record actually carrying a REGISTER/HANDOFF/human-START for that lane; the record, not the instruction text, is the authority a session must check before acting.

lineage_claims.quote: the identical discipline is applied here

rows.anchor: the START GATE REFUSAL ... is the correct verifier behaviour, not a defect; the sole blocker is the missing verification lane
rows.statement: PO/ARB explicitly ratifies the prior gate refusal as correct verifier behaviour rather than a defect, and directs the concrete unblock sequence: Governance REGISTER the verification lane → HANDOFF → human START → only then may the appointed verifier act.

rows.anchor: It would be a duplicate of completed, recorded work ... Re-running it adds no governed value ... This process has no lane.
rows.statement: A second fresh process refuses to re-verify already-completed, already-recorded work, extending the gate-refusal doctrine with a new ground: re-running a governed step that has already concluded and been recorded would itself be an unlaned act presented as a governed act, worsening rather than fixing the outstanding provenance/durability problems.

rows.anchor: this process IS the CORRECTION-001 author — lane seq 1→3, role architecture ... A process that is the Architecture author cannot credibly make that confirmation about itself
rows.statement: The correction author refuses to perform the Governance adoption review of its own correction, extending the producer-bar principle (a producer never verifies or accepts its own work) specifically to bar an author from performing or recommending the adoption-readiness review of that same work.

rows.anchor: This process is not identity-disqualified ... The gate fails for a different, and decisive, reason: the governed lane does not exist ... the block is the missing lane, not the identity of the would-be reviewer
rows.statement: A fresh, fully identity-clean candidate reviewer is still refused for the Governance adoption review, isolating lane-absence as a standalone blocking condition independent of any particular candidate's identity, and confirming the recorded sequence cannot be advanced merely by handing the prompt to a different process.

rows.anchor: the PO/ARB appointment of d31ea60f is not confirmable from any authoritative record — it exists only as text inside the prompt ... Recording a recordedBy: human START on the strength of a prompt would fabricate a human authority act (G-3 boundary) and write an irreversible mutation into the trust anchor
rows.statement: A process refuses an instruction to write REGISTER/HANDOFF/human-START for a named appointee because the appointment itself is unrecorded (exists only as prompt text, with no workflow transition, grant, or registration artifact), and because writing an irreversible human-START transition on that basis would fabricate a human authority act and corrupt the trust anchor every resolver (AST-015/016/017) relies on.

rows.anchor: the START GATE REFUSALs by b51dba91 and d31ea60f are the correct Governance-reviewer behaviour under the gate, not defects; the missing object was a recorded PO/ARB appointment + an authorized governance-recording act, both now supplied by this ruling
rows.statement: PO/ARB appoints d31ea60f as Governance adoption reviewer and directs the exact unblock sequence (REGISTER→HANDOFF→human-START, seq 7-9), explicitly re-affirming both prior refusals as correct behaviour and naming the recorded appointment plus authorized recording act as the two things that were missing.

rows.anchor: The human START act recorded at seq 3 declares its own sequence verbatim ... The STOP that the governed sequence places before 'fresh independent verifier' has not been recorded. The work item is therefore not yet at the point in its own declared sequence where a verifier is due
rows.statement: Beyond the missing verification lane, a second and independent gate failure is identified: the predecessor implementation lane was never explicitly STOPPED per its own recorded declared sequence, so appointing a verifier while that lane still holds mutationOwner would leave the record internally inconsistent — two separately-necessary facts are missing, not one.

rows.anchor: This is at least the seventh recorded gate refusal caused by a commissioning prompt asserting a lane the record does not carry.
rows.statement: The refusing process itself counts the recurrence of the gate-refusal pattern (at least seven instances by this point) and explicitly declines to judge whether the pattern warrants a governance remedy, leaving that classification to Governance.

rows.anchor: But under the improved operating model, this is precisely the capability we should add: a genuinely fresh, pre-commissioned session may bind its own discovered runtime identity to its already-authorized role, then enter the normal REGISTER → HANDOFF → human START sequence.
rows.statement: The fresh verifier's earlier gate refusal is re-interpreted: it was correct behaviour under the old (self-registration-prohibited) flow, but under the newly proposed flow the same scenario becomes exactly the capability the platform should now add, rather than a defect to keep refusing forever.

rows.anchor: If the verifier also performed the adoption review, VERIFIED and ADOPTED-review would collapse into one actor — the exact collapse the operating model forbids.
rows.statement: The verifier itself refuses to perform the Governance adoption review, extending the producer-bar/separation-of-duties chain a further step: a verifier acting as its own adoption reviewer would collapse two of the operating model's four distinct states (VERIFIED, ADOPTED) into a single actor's judgement, which §38 explicitly forbids.

rows.anchor: this process is the CORRECTION-001 author of this estate ... it also holds no governed lane on this work item at all
rows.statement: A second, independent refusal on the same Governance-adoption-review step (following the verifier's own refusal in S0351) shows a candidate barred on two grounds at once — a cross-work-item identity bar (correction author of a related work item) and total lane-absence on this work item — confirming the recurring common blocker is the missing role=governance lane.

sources.note: A 2026-09-07 evidence paper (input to governance decision OQ-1) measuring two actively-running code carriers (A: zero-algebra's Rep/Item ladder R1-R4; B: knowledgeos-sim's per-concern typed dataclasses matching a prior structured-epistemic-object correction), identifying one narrow 'reason channel' seam between them, tabulating ten total carrier candidates (three with executed results), and self-correcting in place (5b) after the same-day OQ-4 witness experiment revealed a third record type. Superseded in carrier-count (not conclusion) by oq1-carrier-decision-brief-2026-09's finding of three implemented carriers.

rows.anchor: Theory 13 §1: 'KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier. Every result was produced on r=(value,source,tag,time) with |D|<=6.' Measured against the code, both halves of that sentence need correction. 'no declared carrier' -> THREE code estates run on three declared carriers ... The carrier is not missing. It exists twice, in two shapes, and Theory 13 UNDERSTATES the one it names. OQ-1 is therefore a RECONCILE-or-RATIFY decision, not a choose-from-nothing decision.
rows.statement: Corrects Theory 13's claim of 'no declared mathematical carrier' by measuring code estates that actually run on declared carriers, reframing OQ-1 from a choose-from-nothing decision into a reconcile-or-ratify decision over carriers that already exist and already run experiments.

lineage_claims.quote: Measured against the code, both halves of that sentence need correction.

rows.anchor: Carrier A -- the zero-algebra estate: verification/zero-algebra/, 59 .py, 53 .json, 50 .md, 22 experiment directories. @dataclass Item: token, source, uncertainty, scope, polarity, node, edge_to (7 fields). @dataclass Rep: cls (R1|R2|R3|R4), items. Carrier A = Rep=(cls,(Item_1,...,Item_n)), Item has 7 fields. And it is a LADDER, not a single level: R1 token only (old generator violated its own R1 declaration in 40.2% of cases), R2 token+within-case rank in {1,2,3}, R3 token+2-significant-digit value (rounding creates ties; ranks cannot), R4 fuller representation.
rows.statement: Defines Carrier A precisely from verbatim code: a Rep(cls, Item-tuple) with a 7-field Item dataclass, organized as an R1-R4 representation ladder (token-only through fuller representation), noting the old generator itself violated its R1 declaration in 40.2% of cases.

rows.anchor: Consequence already proven on this carrier: E_S(D) = D\S is invalid at R2 -- removing an item from a rank vector leaves ranks {2,3}, which is not a valid rank vector. Set subtraction is not the elimination primitive. (PROGRAMME-STATUS-2026-09-03, Correction 1.) What runs on it: the Zero, representation-reduction, bridge and zoom families -- the [EXP] results Theory 13 describes, including the three separations, FR-001, and the 2026-09-07 finding that Zero is not an element property.
rows.statement: Restates a previously-proven consequence specific to Carrier A: plain set subtraction E_S(D)=D\S is invalid at level R2 because removing an item from a rank vector produces an invalid rank vector, confirming set subtraction is not the correct elimination primitive; lists the whole Zero/reduction/bridge/zoom experimental family, including this same batch's OQ-4 witness finding, as running on Carrier A.

rows.anchor: Carrier B -- the v1.2 simulation estate: research/knowledgeos-sim/, 55 .py, 109 .json, verified to run this session. No single record type. Per-concern frozen dataclasses: EVal(value,reason,evaluator,dependencies,contradiction,provenance_state,temporal_state,operational_state,theory_status,domain_restricted,trace); Arg(id,rel [a typed relation, not a signed scalar],weight,source,derived_from,about); State(args,hypotheses,admissible,truth [truth=ORACLE ONLY]); Boundary(kind,cls,reason,remediable_by,blocking); plus Situation/ActionTheory/World/Regime for the Reiter/multiplicity/distinguishability families.
rows.statement: Defines Carrier B as a set of per-concern typed dataclasses (EVal, Arg, State, Boundary, plus Situation/ActionTheory/World/Regime) rather than a single record type, explicitly noting Arg.rel is a typed relation (not a signed scalar) and State.truth is oracle-only.

rows.anchor: Field frequency across the estate: provenance 41, source 37, context 28, time 27, status 23, content 19, evidence 14, value 10. That field set is 37's structured epistemic object k=(id,content,context,evidence,provenance,uncertainty,status) -- the correction the corpus made to itself on 2026-09-01, already implemented in code on 2026-09-02. Carrier B is not a proposal; it is running. What runs on it: the 26 named v1.2 experiments -- Sat, Zero readings, factivity, Contr/FDE, closure, history, multiplicity, N_eff, distinguishability, Hilbert, composition.
rows.statement: Measures Carrier B's actual field frequency across the codebase and shows it matches a previously-recorded structured epistemic object k=(id,content,context,evidence,provenance,uncertainty,status) from a 2026-09-01 self-correction, demonstrating that correction was already implemented in code by 2026-09-02 rather than remaining a proposal; lists 26 named v1.2 experiments running on Carrier B.

rows.anchor: The one seam -- and it is narrow: Carrier A (Rep(cls,Item...), a REPRESENTATION being transformed/reduced) feeds Carrier B (EVal/Arg/State, an EVALUATION over content, with reasons) -- the seam: what does an evaluator receive? Carries a REASON? Carrier A: no. Carrier B: yes -- reason, remediable_by, trace. The seam is the reason channel. Carrier A can say WHAT was removed. Only Carrier B can say WHY.
rows.statement: Identifies the single narrow seam between Carrier A and Carrier B as a pipeline relationship (A produces representations, B evaluates them) whose only missing link is a 'reason channel': Carrier A can state what was removed but has no field for why, while Carrier B carries reason/remediable_by/trace.

rows.anchor: And that is the same channel three independent results demanded: KR-CONTR-FDE's two boundary collapses ('Standing has no channel for why') · KR-CONTR-EVAL's theorem that no flat domain of any cardinality is adequate and the minimum is a pair with an indispensable reason/boundary component · and Boundary.remediable_by itself. A carrier decision that keeps A and B separate must declare the seam's contract. A carrier decision that unifies them must give Rep a reason channel. Those are the two shapes of OQ-1, and this paper does not choose between them.
rows.statement: Argues the reason-channel seam is independently corroborated by three separate prior results (KR-CONTR-FDE's boundary collapses, KR-CONTR-EVAL's minimum-adequate-domain theorem, and Boundary.remediable_by itself), and frames OQ-1 as reducing to exactly two shapes: declare the seam contract (keep A/B separate) or add a reason channel to Rep (unify them), without choosing between them.

rows.anchor: Carriers DEFINED but carrying no executed result (10-row table): KS=(X,A) measurable epistemic state space, 20 files, none executed; K=(A,R) the verification lane's kernel, 98 files, kos_kernel.py 29 experiments -- executed; ratified K_t over 8 primitives, 41 files, no code; K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) 6 fields, 7 files, none; Theory-01 D,T,R,Q,Pi,O,C,E_S, 121 files, = Carrier A's vocabulary -- executed; Sigma 5-axis 2240 states, 112 files, partly executed, 0 of 5 axes ordered; D_t varying dimension set, 18 files, none, population rule blocked; G_t=(V,E,Phi) attributed multigraph, 5 files, none, its convergence theorem found invalid; h_Lambda=(H,R_sem,Lambda,Sigma_Lambda) FR-001's [PROP] successor, 7 files, none; Hilbert-space representation KR-HILBERT, 37 files, negative result (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED weakest sense, H1/H3/H7/H8 refuted). Ten candidates. THREE carry executed results. Two of those three are Carriers A and B.
rows.statement: Tabulates ten total carrier candidates found across the corpus, of which only three carry any executed result (K=(A,R)/Carrier A's kernel, Theory-01's vocabulary matching Carrier A, and the negative Hilbert-space result), with the ratified K_t itself among the seven with no executed result.
